item.content:encoded:
Dodgers doblegan Giants
Mookie Betts batea de 4-4 con tres triples y dos impulsadas
El novato dominicano Josué De Paula pega sencillo impulsador de 2 carreras, anota dos y recibe dos bases por bolas
LOS ÁNGELES.— Mookie Betts bateó de 4-4 con tres dobles, Will Smith agregó tres hits, incluyendo un jonrón, y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles vencieron a los Gigantes de San Francisco 10-4 el sábado por la noche.
El sencillo de dos carreras con dos outs de Tommy Edman ante el relevista Philip Abner rompió el empate a 4 en la quinta entrada. El bateador emergente Miguel Rojas conectó un sencillo productor para poner el marcador 7-4 a favor de su equipo, y Edman fue puesto out en el plato para finalizar la entrada.
Todos los Dodgers conectaron al menos un hit, excepto Freddie Freeman, quien tuvo un mal desempeño y se fue de 0 de 5. Betts igualó su mejor marca de la temporada en hits y el equipo superó a los Giants en jonrones, 15-8. El ex Jugador Más Valioso de la Liga Americana bateaba .249 hace una semana y desde entonces ha elevado su promedio a .261.
Los Dodgers anotaron carreras en seis entradas consecutivas al inicio de un partido por primera vez en 10 años. Han anotado 15 carreras en sus últimas siete entradas ofensivas, incluyendo cuatro jonrones en la octava entrada contra Abner en el primer partido de la serie del viernes.
Los campeones de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional (95-60) ganaron su partido número 95 para colocarse 35 juegos por encima del .500, su mejor marca de la temporada.
El tercer doble de Betts abrió la sexta entrada y anotó con un sencillo productor de Smith ante el relevista Joel Kuhnel. El novato Josue De Paula añadió un sencillo productor de dos carreras, ampliando la ventaja a 10-4.
En tres ocasiones, los Giants remontaron para empatar el partido, solo para ver cómo los Dodgers volvían a tomar la delantera, destacando el jonrón de dos carreras de Victor Bericoto, de 425 pies, que empató el partido en la tercera entrada.
El abridor de los Dodgers, Tarik Skubal (11-7), no estuvo especialmente brillante, permitiendo cuatro carreras y ocho hits en cinco entradas. El zurdo ponchó a tres y otorgó dos bases por bolas, y los Dodgers ganaron sus últimas seis salidas.
El relevista Edwin Díaz lanzó una octava entrada sin permitir carreras en su segunda aparición consecutiva desde que salió de la lista de lesionados el viernes.
El abridor de los Giants, Yunior Marte (0-1), permitió seis carreras y ocho hits en 4 2/3 entradas con dos ponches.
El jardinero derecho de los Dodgers, Kyle Tucker, recibió un foul en la rodilla y fue reemplazado por Alex Call en la séptima entrada.

item.title: [pasadenastarnews.com] Mookie Betts stays hot as Dodgers hammer Giants
item.dc:creator: Doug Padilla
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Mookie Betts is showing that the view from the top offers a wide range of possibilities. Hitting in Shohei Ohtani’s leadoff spot for the second consecutive game, Betts’ four-hit performance on Saturday night topped his three-hit output from Friday and started some serious downhill momentum toward a 10-4 victory over the San Francisco Giants. The victory kept the Dodgers (95-60) two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers (97-58) for the best record in the National League and four games
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Mookie Betts is showing that the view from the top offers a wide range of possibilities.
Hitting in Shohei Ohtani’s leadoff spot for the second consecutive game, Betts’ four-hit performance on Saturday night topped his three-hit output from Friday and started some serious downhill momentum toward a 10-4 victory over the San Francisco Giants.
The victory kept the Dodgers (95-60) two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers (97-58) for the best record in the National League and four games ahead of the Atlanta Braves (91-64) for the No. 2 playoff seed with seven games remaining. That includes four games against the Giants, who continue to limp toward the finish line of a miserable, injury-riddled season.
Betts couldn’t be feeling better, with his past two games part of a run of 10 hits over the last three games he has played. After more than two months of looking for an offensive leader, Betts has charged into the role, while reaching base five times on Saturday.
“It’s good; It’s fun,” Betts said. “But the main thing is doing it when it counts. So right now, we just keep laying the foundation, and then when playoffs come, we just need it to show up (offensively).”
The Dodgers expect Ohtani to return for the playoffs as he makes progress from biceps and knee discomfort. Betts, though, is proving to be a more-than-adequate emergency replacement.
“You know, I couldn’t tell you that I saw this (coming), but I just felt that he was stronger,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “He’s worked hard on that. He looks great. He’s not going to stop working, and just for it to come together has been great, and I think for me it’s just trying to keep him confident.”
The Dodgers also have been transformed by the emergence of catcher Will Smith, who returned at the start of September after three months away because of neck inflammation. He had a home run among his three hits Saturday to give him homers in consecutive games, with three over his past eight contests.
“He’ll play two or three that last series (at San Francisco), but yeah, after that, he’ll be our guy (for the playoffs),” Roberts said.
There is also 21-year-old rookie Josue De Paula, who has continued to operate with ease since arriving in the major leagues last week. De Paula had a two-run single Saturday and walked twice while scoring two runs.
All of it overshadowed Tarik Skubal’s ninth start for the Dodgers. The two-time American League Cy Young Award winner was far from his best, allowing four runs on eight hits over five innings. His three strikeouts were his least in an outing with his new club.
Skubal unleashed his frustrations in the dugout by throwing his glove and cap at the bench, while firing an empty sports drink bottle at the wall.
“Sometimes you get frustrated and you got to get it out,” Skubal said. “It’s no good just keeping it pent up. So yeah, I’m a believer in getting that stuff out and kind of just moving on from the moment. The frustration is based on execution and knowing who I am and I’m just not doing that.”
Skubal blamed a lack of fastball command for the inability to shut down the Giants.
“Not driving it up and in (and) kind of pulling the ball down at times, pushing it up at times,” Skubal said. “I think pitching is almost all fastball command and mine wasn’t great today.”
And yet the offense allowed Skubal (11-7) to pick up the win, while improving to 4-2 with a 2.95 ERA for the Dodgers.
“That’s our job. That’s what we’re supposed to do,” Betts said. “So sometimes it’s them, sometimes it’s us. As long as we win.”
Kyle Tucker provided a scare when he fouled a ball off the side of his right knee early in the game then departed in the seventh inning with the Dodgers leading by six runs. Tucker reached base twice Saturday after collecting six hits with two home runs the previous two games.
“Whatever’s working at the time, you just ride it out, whether or not it’s the way you want to go about it,” said Tucker, who expects to play Sunday. “If it’s working, it’s working. You just try to go up there and put up competitive at-bats and just do your part on defense.”
The offense was not only productive, it was steady. The Dodgers scored runs in each of the first six innings and when they were held scoreless in the seventh, Betts still reached base with a walk.
Betts opened the game for the Dodgers with a leadoff double and scored on a Max Muncy double. Betts brought home his own run with an RBI single in the second.
The Dodgers struck with Smith’s home run in the third and got an RBI double from Betts in the fourth but were still tied 4-4 heading into the bottom of the fifth. They blew the game open from there, getting a go-ahead two-run single from Tommy Edman and an RBI pinch-hit single from Miguel Rojas for a 7-4 lead.
They scored three more times in the sixth, getting a Smith RBI single followed by a two-run single from De Paula.
“I think this is the first time, seems like all year, that we’ve had four or five hitters swing the bats well for four or five games,” Roberts said. “So it’s been really good to see. Obviously, Mookie is a big part of it, but everyone else is doing their part.”
The Dodgers now have a 5-4 lead in the Giants in the season series and are in line for a sweep on Sunday, which would be their first against their longtime rival since April of 2024.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers outslug Giants 10-4, led by Mookie Betts with four hits
Mookie Betts had four hits, including three doubles, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 10-4
LOS ANGELES -- Mookie Betts went 4 for 4 with three doubles, Will Smith added three hits including a home run, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 10-4 on Saturday night.
Tommy Edman's two-run, two-out single off reliever Philip Abner snapped a 4-all tie in the fifth. Pinch-hitter Miguel Rojas followed with an RBI single for a 7-4 lead, with Edman thrown out at home to end the inning.
Every Dodger had at least one hit, except for struggling Freddie Freeman who was 0 for 5. Betts tied his season high for hits and the team outslugged the Giants, 15-8. The former AL MVP was hitting .249 a week ago, and has since raised his average to .261.
The Dodgers scored runs in six straight innings to start a game for the first time in 10 years. They've scored 15 runs in their last seven offensive innings, including a four-homer eighth off Abner in Friday's series opener.
The NL West champions (95-60) won their 95th game to move a season-high 35 games above .500.
Betts' third double led off the sixth and he scored on Smith's RBI single off reliever Joel Kuhnel. Rookie Josue De Paula added a two-run RBI single, extending the lead to 10-4.
Three times the Giants rallied to tie the game only to see the Dodgers retake the lead, highlighted by Victor Bericoto's game-tying, 425-foot two-run homer in the third.
Dodgers starter Tarik Skubal (11-7) wasn't particularly sharp, allowing four runs and eight hits in five innings. The left-hander struck out three and walked two, with the Dodgers winning each of his last six outings.
Reliever Edwin Díaz pitched a scoreless eighth in his second straight appearance since coming off the injured list Friday.
Giants starter Yunior Marte (0-1) gave up six runs and eight hits in 4 2/3 innings with two strikeouts.
Dodgers right fielder Kyle Tucker fouled a ball off his knee and was replaced by Alex Call in the seventh.
Neither team had announced their starters for the series finale Sunday.

item.title: [truebluela.com] Dodging a loss in a game of Giant momentum swings

item.description: The Dodgers and San Francisco Giants kept things neck-and-neck through the first half of Saturday night’s contest, but the Dodgers rattled off six unanswered runs in a 10-4 victory. item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers and San Francisco Giants kept things neck-and-neck through the first half of Saturday night’s contest, but the Dodgers rattled off six unanswered runs in a 10-4 victory.
After Tarik Skubal allowed a two-out walk to Giants designated hitter Victor Bericoto, Jung Hoo Lee attacked the first pitch he saw into the right-center field gap, but a diving play from Kyle Tucker got Skubal out of the inning with the game remaining scoreless.
Mookie Betts started things off in the bottom of the first inning with a leadoff double, and Max Muncy cashed him in with a two-strike, two-out RBI double to give the Dodgers the first lead of the game. Betts would come through again in the bottom of the second inning, lacing an RBI single the other way to plate Josue De Paula and make it a 2-0 Dodger lead.
Skubal worked his way around two baserunners for a scoreless top of the second inning, but after allowing a one-out single to Turner Hill in the top of the third inning, Bericoto launched a 3-2 fastball deep over the center field wall, tying the game at 2. Will Smith wasted no time giving the Dodgers the lead again, hammering a solo home run to lead off the bottom of the third inning, giving him his second home run in as many games.
The Giants responded with a pair of leadoff singles from Andrew Knizner and Osleivis Basabe to begin the top of the fourth inning. A bunt from Christian Koss moved both men into scoring position, and a squeeze bunt from Jonah Cox plated Knizner to tie the game at 3.
The Dodgers would get another one-run lead thanks to an RBI double from Mookie Betts in the bottom of the fourth inning— his second double and second RBI of the game. The Giants wouldn’t let Skubal settle in for the top of the fifth inning, as Bericoto and Lee both doubled to tie the game at four.
Saturday turned out to be Skubal’s worst outing of the season, let alone as a Dodger. Skubal managed to complete five innings of work but allowed a season-high four earned runs, while his three strikeouts on the night were the fewest in any start since striking out three on August 14 of last season against the Minnesota Twins.
Despite the poor start, the Dodgers put Skubal officially in line for the win as Teoscar Hernández ignited a two-out rally with an opposite-field single. Kyle Tucker and Josue De Paula each followed with a walk, and Tommy Edman snapped out of a 1-37 funk with a go-ahead, two-run single to give the Dodgers their first multi-run lead since the third. Miguel Rojas knocked a pinch-hit single to bring home De Paula, but Edman was thrown out at home attempting to make it a four-run inning.
Evan Phillips recorded the first clean inning of the night in relief of Skubal in the top of the sixth inning, and the Dodgers responded with another three-run inning, capitalized by a two-run single by De Paula and giving the Dodgers a six-run cushion.
After a scoreless inning from Alex Vesia in the seventh inning, Edwin Díaz came in for his second consecutive game since returning from injury, pitching a scoreless top of the eighth inning while picking up a pair of strikeouts.
Mookie Betts finished Saturday going 4-4 with three doubles and two RBI, reaching base five times after a walk in the seventh inning. Betts is now 10-12 (.833 average) over his last three games with three doubles, two home runs and five RBI.
With their win over the Giants, the Dodgers maintain a four-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the no. 2 seed in the National League. They still trail the Milwaukee Brewers by two games for the top seed.
Game particulars
- Home runs— Victor Bericoto (5); Will Smith (9)
- WP— Tarik Skubal (11-7): 5 IP, 8 hits, 4 earned runs, 2 walks, 3 strikeouts
- LP— Yunior Marte (0-1): 4 2/3 IP, 8 hits, 6 earned runs, 3 walks, 2 strikeouts
Up next
The Dodgers wrap things up against San Francisco on Sunday (1:10 p.m. PT, SportsNet LA) before hosting the San Diego Padres for their final regular season home series beginning Tuesday. Both teams have yet to announce their starters.

item.content:encoded:
Mookie Betts se fue de 4-4 con tres dobles, Will Smith añadió tres imparables, incluido un jonrón, y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles vencieron la noche del sábado por 10-4 a los Gigantes de San Francisco.
El sencillo de Tommy Edman de dos carreras con dos outs ante el relevista Philip Abner rompió el empate 4-4 en la quinta. El bateador emergente venezolano Miguel Rojas siguió con un sencillo impulsor para poner el marcador 7-4, y Edman fue puesto out en el plato para terminar la entrada.
Todos los Dodgers conectaron al menos un hit, excepto el alicaído Freddie Freeman, que se fue de 5-0. Betts igualó su máximo de la temporada en hits y el equipo superó a los Giants en batazos, 15-8. El ex MVP de la Liga Americana bateaba para .249 hace una semana, y desde entonces elevó su promedio a .261.
El abridor de los Dodgers, Tarik Skubal (11-7), permitió cuatro carreras y ocho hits en cinco entradas.
El relevista boricua Edwin Díaz lanzó una octava entrada sin carreras en su segunda aparición consecutiva desde que salió de la lista de lesionados el viernes.
El abridor dominicano de los Gigantes, Yunior Marte (0-1), permitió seis carreras y ocho hits en 4 2/3 entradas, con dos ponches.

item.title: [MARCA] Ohtani ramps up hitting progression: Why Dave Roberts is bullish on star's October return
item.dc:creator: Adriano Boin
item.description: - Los Angeles Dodgers. Dodgers facing nightmare playoff decision over Edwin Díaz as October looms - Los Angeles Dodgers. “They basically lie”: Shohei Ohtani accused of hiding multiple injuries to avoid being placed on Dodgers' injured list Shohei Ohtani’s path back to the Los Angeles Dodgers lineup is becoming clearer, and manager Dave Roberts has provided another encouraging sign as the club prepares for October. Ohtani took coach-pitch batting practice Friday after beginning his hitting progre
item.content:encoded:
- Los Angeles Dodgers. Dodgers facing nightmare playoff decision over Edwin Díaz as October looms
- Los Angeles Dodgers. “They basically lie”: Shohei Ohtani accused of hiding multiple injuries to avoid being placed on Dodgers' injured list
Shohei Ohtani’s path back to the Los Angeles Dodgers lineup is becoming clearer, and manager Dave Roberts has provided another encouraging sign as the club prepares for October.
Ohtani took coach-pitch batting practice Friday after beginning his hitting progression with tee work earlier in the week. The Dodgers’ four-time MVP remains on the 15-day injured list with left-knee and right-biceps issues, but his recent activity has given the club reason for optimism.
Roberts said Ohtani came through the latest workout well and described the past several days as productive. However, the manager stressed that the slugger hasn’t yet advanced to live batting practice or work with the Trajekt pitching simulator.
“He came out of it well,” Roberts said. “I think for me, I'm just really waiting to hear when he's going to get on the field, let alone take live BP or Trajekt.
“And he's not there yet. But everything I've heard, it's been a really productive last three to four to five days. He's in a good spot.”
Before Ohtani returns to game action, Roberts wants him to face roughly 10 to 12 at-bats against pitching.
That timetable matters. Ohtani’s IL stint was backdated to Sept. 8, making Sept. 23 the earliest activation date. If he’s ready by then, he’ll have only five regular-season games to regain his timing before the postseason begins.
Dodgers’ offense keeps rolling without Ohtani
The Dodgers have managed his absence effectively, winning six of nine games and averaging 5.3 runs per contest during that stretch. Their latest victory showed just how much offensive depth remains available while Ohtani recovers.
Los Angeles defeated the San Francisco Giants 8-2 on Friday, with Mookie Betts homering twice and the Dodgers launching four home runs in the eighth inning.
Max Muncy and Kyle Tucker went back-to-back before Betts and Will Smith followed with consecutive blasts. Tyler Glasnow also delivered six innings with 10 strikeouts.
The performance underscored why the Dodgers can afford to be patient with Ohtani rather than rushing his return. Still, his presence would add another major dimension to a lineup already producing at a high level.
Before landing on the injured list, Ohtani hit .296 with 26 home runs and a .952 OPS across 110 games. He struggled over his final 24 games, batting .198 with a .690 OPS and 34 strikeouts, making the decision to pause his workload especially significant.
Ohtani’s return date remains unconfirmed, but the progression from tee work to coach-pitch batting practice represents another step forward.
With Los Angeles already having secured the NL West, the priority is getting its superstar healthy and ready to contribute when the games carry their greatest postseason significance.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Edgardo Henriquez avoids the worst, but Dodgers still making promises they can’t keep
item.dc:creator: Evan Roberts

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are constantly hoping for the best for their injured players, despite some signs that they might not be themselves come October.
The National League West champions currently have back-to-back NL MVP Shohei Ohtani on the injured list, and Dave Roberts recently said that "he's feeling normal...ish" after reporting they are hoping to activate him when first eligible.
Former Cy Young Award-winner Blake Snell also is dealing with an injury, and the Dodgers are hoping for the best with him as well. First baseman Freddie Freeman is working through a knee injury that caused him to experience a major dip in production.
Freeman has looked more like himself in recent days, but the larger concern is the myriad contributors who are working their way back from injuries right before the playoffs. Dodgers fans should add the team's best reliever to that group of players that LA's coaching staff swears will be fine.
Edgardo Henriquez avoids the worst, but Dodgers still making promises they can’t keep
Edgardo Henriquez landed on the injured list last week with a low-grade back strain — the Dodgers correspondingly promoted Bobby Miller to the active roster — and it was reported that LA's right-hander has no structural damage. Unsurprisingly, the Dodgers still think he'll be back before the season ends!
Whether he could or he should, there is simply no way of knowing what the best path forward is for Henriquez and the Dodgers. Los Angeles needs him sharp and healthy once the calendar flips to October, but it seems that bringing him back before the playoffs will sacrifice one of those things.
Henriquez has been one of the best relievers in baseball this season, hands-down. He is one of 67 pitchers with 60-plus appearances this season -- of that group, Henriquez ranks 10th in FIP (2.52), fifth in batting average against (.177), second in slugging percentage (.239), fourth in OPS (.523), and is tied for first in home runs allowed (one).
While most fans assumed that Edwin Diaz and Tanner Scott would be the Dodgers most reliable relievers, the stats show that Henriquez and Alex Vesia have been far steadier coming out of the bullpen.

item.dc:creator: Por Servicios combinados
item.description: En el partido de regreso la recta de Edwin Díaz promedió 97.6 millas por hora, 1.3 millas por arriba de lo que era su promedio en la temporada, pero alcanzó en el juego las 99 mph. (Mark J. item.content:encoded:
En el partido de regreso la recta de Edwin Díaz promedió 97.6 millas por hora, 1.3 millas por arriba de lo que era su promedio en la temporada, pero alcanzó en el juego las 99 mph. (Mark J. Terrill)
Por Servicios combinados
Los Ángeles - Mookie Betts conectó dos jonrones y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles pegaron cuatro cuadrangulares en la octava entrada para imponerse 8-2 a los Giants de San Francisco la noche del viernes, en un partido que marcó el regreso desde la lista de lesionados del relevista puertorriqueño Edwin “Sugar” Díaz.
Max Muncy y Kyle Tucker conectaron jonrones consecutivos en la octava. Betts y Max Muncy añadieron vuelacercas solitarios con dos outs en una entrada de cinco carreras, mientras los campeones del Oeste de la Liga Nacional se impusieron en el primer juego de una serie entre viejos rivales.
Tyler Glasnow (5-1) permitió dos carreras y tres imparables en seis entradas, con un máximo de temporada de 10 ponches.
La lluvia de jonrones ocurrió en el vigésimo aniversario del juego de cuatro-más-uno de los Dodgers. Jeff Kent, J.D. Drew, Russell Martin y Marlon Anderson conectaron cuatro jonrones consecutivos en la parte baja de la novena entrada, la cuarta vez en la historia de las Grandes Ligas que se lograba esa hazaña.
El relevista de los Giants Philip Abner permitió las cinco carreras en la octava, que comenzó con los Dodgers arriba 3-2. Se convirtió en el segundo relevista en la historia de San Francisco en permitir cuatro jonrones en una misma entrada.
Los Giants (64-90) perdieron su juego número 90, su mayor cantidad desde 2017, cuando cayeron 98 veces.
El boricua Edwin Díaz ponchó a dos en una novena entrada sin carreras en su regreso desde la lista de lesionados.
Los Dodgers lo activaron desde la lista de lesionados de 15 días, donde había ingresado el 18 de agosto por una inflamación en el cuello. Fue su segunda vez en el año en la lista de lesionados, luego de una primera por problemas en el codo derecho.
El equipo no espera usar al relevista en situaciones de aprietos, pero con ventaja de seis carreras fue traído en la novena. De no haber sido por esa ventaja, admitió el dirigente Dave Roberts, no lo hubieran utilizado en la novena.
Provocó un elevado y ponchó a un bateador con un foul tip antes de permitir un sencillo con dos outs. Pero evitó cualquier daño, terminando el juego al hacer que Brett Harris hiciera swing a un slider difícil de batear. La recta de cuatro costuras de Díaz promedió 97.6 millas por hora (1.3 mph más que su promedio de la temporada), alcanzando un máximo de 98.7 millas.
“La recta tenía mucha vida”, dijo Roberts según publicó MLB.com. “Noventa y seis millas por hora es muy diferente a 99. Y parecía que su lanzamiento pasaba por el receptor, y la recta tenía esa potencia. Y luego el slider... una vez que tienes esa recta, el slider es bastante letal”.

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts wants to see Edwin Diaz perform up to par.
Roberts spoke to the media on Thursday, a day before the Dodgers activated Diaz, and challenged him to prove he can be the closer they signed to a massive deal this past winter.
“I think, like anything, it should be a meritocracy,” Roberts said of the team's bullpen. “You have to earn the right of opportunities, but then you also have to perform, right? Eddie understands that. I think where we’re at now we just need guys to buy in, perform and go from there. That’s what he’s about.”
Diaz was activated on Friday. In a corresponding move, the Dodgers optioned right-handed pitcher Landon Knack.
The All-Star closer has had a frustrating season. Entering Friday night, the right-hander had appeared in only 16 games this season, recording an abysmal 11.35 ERA, 2.56 WHIP and 19 strikeouts in 13.2 innings.
Los Angeles made Diaz the highest-paid closer by average annual salary, but the investment has yet to pay off.
The 32-year-old has blown four saves out of 11 opportunities, while batters were hitting a staggering .385 against him in Los Angeles heading into Friday night's game.
On Friday night, Diaz entered in the six-run game in the ninth inning, and had a scoreless inning with two strikeouts.
Injuries have certainly played a role in what has been a disappointing season for Diaz. He missed significant time following elbow surgery and has recently been sidelined by neck inflammation.
The combination of inconsistency on the mound, injuries and a lack of results has cast serious doubt over whether Diaz will even make the Dodgers' postseason roster.
Will Edwin Diaz Make the Dodgers’ Postseason Roster?
With a little over a week until the end of the regular season, Roberts and the Dodgers will have to make a tough decision.
Diaz looked good in his first outing, and he'll likely have three or four more to prove he deserves a spot on the postseson roster.
“Quality of strike-throwing. Get guys out,” Roberts said in regards to what he hopes to see from Diaz. “That’s probably it. As you get into the postseason, every inning’s leverage. So that’s kind of it. Quality of strike-throwing, and get guys out.”
The Dodgers skipper said they will use Diaz in low-leverage situations to ramp him up, and he'll have to earn more high-profile assignments.
If Diaz can find his form over the next week or so, the Dodgers could be in a much better position to chase their third straight World Series title this October.

item.content:encoded:
With just over one week left in the regular season, the Los Angeles Dodgers are still looking to secure the No. 2 seed in the National League postseason bracket and perhaps more importantly, get to a better state of health.
Edwin Díaz returned from the injured list on Friday, but the Dodgers are still waiting on the likes of Andy Pages, Dalton Rushing, Roki Sasaki and Shohei Ohtani. Fortunately for L.A., there is optimism with that group, and Blake Snell as well after he came out his most recent start due to left groin tightness.
Dodgers updates
Blake Snell
Snell played catch from flat ground on Friday, getting out to 90 feet as signs point to avoiding the 15-day injured list.
“I’m very hopeful that he’ll make a start before the end of the season,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said.
Snell has a history of missing roughly one month because of adductor/groin strains, but he and the team believe the latest issue did not advance to being that significant.
“Don’t know the answer exactly,” Roberts said when asked what may have caused the tightness, “but happy that we caught it early.”
If — or when — Snell does pitch again, Roberts indicated it would be a normal start rather than an abbreviated final tuneup before the postseason begins.
Andy Pages
After previously sharing the expectation is for Pages to return during the homestand, Roberts offered a slightly more concrete timeline by saying that should come during the Dodgers’ series against the San Diego Padres.
Dalton Rushing
According to Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic, Rushing received a PRP injection in his right forearm.
Dalton Rushing got a PRP injection a week ago to address his flexor in his right arm. Still holding out hope he can be an option as a bat going forward — will hit off a machine in the coming days to test it out.
Surgery still doesn’t appear on the table yet.
— Fabian Ardaya (@FabianArdaya) September 18, 2026
Rushing had a brief return at the start of September after going on the 10-day injured list last month because of a slight tear in the UCL of his right elbow. The Dodgers have suggested a best-case scenario is to have Rushing available as a pinch-hit option off the bench in the playoffs.
Shohei Ohtani
Ohtani took swings against a coach pitching in the batting cage and “came out of it well,” per Roberts. Although the superstar talent is making progress, Roberts said more clarity won’t come until Ohtani faces live pitching or hits off the Trajekt machine.
“But everything I’ve heard, it’s been a really productive last three to four to five days. He’s in a good spot,” Roberts added.
Roki Sasaki
Roberts further confirmed Sasaki is nearing a return and will start despite the prior plan being to shift him into a bullpen role. Some of the change is due to the uncertainty that arose from Snell’s groin trouble.
However, Sasaki still figures to be utilized as a reliever in the postseason if the Dodgers rotation remains healthy.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers got to see Edwin Diaz in action for the first time since a tumultuous stint in Triple-A, and his outing inspired confidence.
Diaz, who was activated on Friday, returned to the majors the same day, ending a month on the sidelines.
He didn’t warm up until the Dodgers lit up the San Francisco Giants for five runs in the eighth inning, creating an 8-2 gap and a low-leverage chance for the Puerto Rican.
Then, Diaz got up, and eventually, the trumpets sounded at the top of the ninth inning.
He came in and had a good outing, allowing just one hit, no walks, and two punchouts.
More importantly than anything, there were no hard-hit balls for Diaz, something that he has struggled with, while avoiding walks.
Diaz’s fastball was the star of the show. It improved compared to earlier in the season, with 1.3 mph more on the pitch and an extra inch of horizontal and vertical break, according to Baseball Savant.
Not only did the pitch move well, but he controlled it well too. Diaz’s slider delivered well in terms of results, getting a 50% chase rate.
The slider had less drop and horizontal break by an inch each, something to monitor going forward, but based on just the game, it was good enough to complement the fastball.
Why Edwin Diaz needed a good outing
Diaz had two different stints on the injured list, one for his elbow surgery and another for neck inflammation, and has been bad at pretty much every turn.
In the major leagues, Diaz was riding an 11.85 ERA through 13.2 innings with a 5.81 FIP, signaling consistent struggles, per Baseball-Reference.
During his latest minor league stint, things were ugly again. He pitched 4.1 innings in Triple-A and posted an 11.00 ERA.
Given how things looked all year for Diaz, with more bad outings than good, the fanbase feared giving him another chance, and even Dave Roberts, who seemingly loves Diaz based on their interactions, challenged Diaz to produce good outings.
After Friday’s return, Roberts was quite happy.
“I think getting strike one, I think the fastball had that life, 96 is a lot different than 99, and it just seemed like his delivery was through the catcher, and the slider, once you have that fastball, the slider is pretty lethal,” Roberts said.
“He’ll be available tomorrow and we are trying to get him four or five start or outings before the end of the season.”
During those next outings, Diaz’s slider and results will remain under a microscope.

item.content:encoded:
That's one way to start off the last homestand of the regular season.
Forget the fact that it was against the lowly San Francisco Giants and their lineup featuring a who's who of ... "Who?" Forget the fact that five of the Los Angeles Dodgers' runs in their dominant 8-2 win on Friday night came off the relatively unknown Philip Abner. The Dodgers' lineup, without Shohei Ohtani, showed exactly what they're capable of offensively.
This is the version of the team Andrew Friedman envisioned when he signed Kyle Tucker to a four-year, $240 million contract and Edwin Díaz to a three-year, $69 million deal last winter.
"The talent," manager Dave Roberts said. "It's a high-floor talent level. I just like the way we're taking better team at-bats and making up for not having Shohei in there. Obviously, we're a better team with him, but it is nice to see there hasn't been a drop-off with him not in the lineup."
Here's a look at three winners from the Dodgers' victory over the Giants:
The Dodgers lineup is just fine
Mookie Betts started things off when he jumped on a low-90s fastball that San Francisco starter Cesar Perdomo left middle-middle and sent it over the fence in left center field for his 33rd leadoff home run as a Dodger. The bats went quiet briefly from there until the bottom of the fifth when Teoscar Hernández singled home Josue De Paula from third on a sharp liner to right field to tie the game at 2-2.
The rookie De Paula later drove in the go-ahead run on an RBI double in the sixth before a monster five-run eighth inning in which Max Muncy, Tucker, Betts and Will Smith all went yard to put the game out of reach.
"I think that's the beauty in it," Betts said. "We just keep giving ourselves opportunities and eventually, something will crack. It did tonight, so we just have to keep getting guys on base and giving ourselves the chances and the hits will follow."
Edwin Díaz looked good in return from IL
That set the stage for the trumpets to once again blare over the Dodger Stadium loudspeakers. Roberts said he wouldn't have put Díaz in if it wasn't for the six-run lead as he wanted to give Díaz some leeway in his first outing back from an IL stint after health and poor performance have plagued his season.
But Díaz took the opportunity and ran with it. In his first big league appearance since Aug. 17, he got two quick outs before giving up a base hit up the middle. Rather than let that snowball like it has many times in 2026, however, Díaz was able to buckle down and strike out Brett Harris on three pitches to seal a Dodgers win.
"I liked everything," Roberts said. "I liked his intensity; I liked the fastball velocity. The slider was good. It was just really good to get him back in the mix and that's something to build on."
Josue De Paula is different
The through line for the offense on Friday night was the 21-year-old De Paula. The No. 6 prospect in baseball according to MLB Pipeline finished the night 2-for-3 with a walk, two runs and an RBI, but it was the timing of each of those that made his Dodger Stadium debut so special.
De Paula led off the bottom of the fifth with a base hit, which Betts followed up with one of his own before he eventually scored the tying run on Hernández's RBI single. Two innings later, De Paula scored Tucker from first on a double that he put on a rope at 107 mph deep into the right field gap. As he reached second, De Paula pounded his chest and flexed.
Then, in that huge eighth inning, it was De Paula who kept it alive by working a four-pitch walk with two outs, his seventh in a week in the big leagues. Five pitches later, Betts blew the game open with a two-run homer.
"I just love his at-bats," Roberts said. "It's one of those things that we knew coming up to the big leagues, he wasn't going to get overwhelmed, and it just helps when you control the strike zone. He takes his walks, when the ball is in the hitting zone, he can slug you but he also knows how to get a base hit. It's been very professional."

item.content:encoded:
Mookie Betts pega 2 jonrones y Dodgers conectan 4 en la 8va en triunfo ante Gigantes
LOS ÁNGELES — Mookie Betts conectó dos jonrones y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles pegaron cuatro cuadrangulares en la octava entrada para imponerse 8-2 a los Gigantes de San Francisco la noche del viernes.
Max Muncy y Kyle Tucker conectaron jonrones consecutivos en la octava. Betts y Max Muncy añadieron vuelacercas solitarios con dos outs en una entrada de cinco carreras, mientras los campeones del Oeste de la Liga Nacional se impusieron en el primer juego de una serie entre viejos rivales.
Tyler Glasnow (5-1) permitió dos carreras y tres imparables en seis entradas, con un máximo de temporada de 10 ponches.
La lluvia de jonrones ocurrió en el 20mo aniversario del juego de cuatro-más-uno de los Dodgers. Jeff Kent, J.D. Drew, Russell Martin y Marlon Anderson conectaron cuatro jonrones consecutivos en la parte baja de la novena entrada, la cuarta vez en la historia de las Grandes Ligas que se lograba esa hazaña.
El relevista de los Gigantes Philip Abner permitió las cinco carreras en la octava, que comenzó con los Dodgers arriba 3-2. Se convirtió en el segundo relevista en la historia de San Francisco en permitir cuatro jonrones en una misma entrada.
Los Gigantes (64-90) perdieron su juego número 90, su mayor cantidad desde 2017, cuando cayeron 98 veces.
El boricua Edwin Díaz ponchó a dos en una novena entrada sin carreras en su regreso desde la lista de lesionados.
El abridor de los Gigantes Cesar Perdomo permitió dos carreras y seis hits en 4 2/3 entradas, con un ponche. Jason Foley (3-2) cargó con la derrota como relevista. ___

item.title: [bozemandailychronicle.com] Mookie Betts homers twice and Dodgers hit 4 in 8th inning of 8-2 win over Giants
item.dc:creator: BETH HARRIS
item.description: LOS ANGELES (AP) — Mookie Betts homered twice and the Los Angeles Dodgers went deep four times in the eighth inning of an 8-2 victory over the San Francisco Giants on Friday night. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Mookie Betts homered twice and the Los Angeles Dodgers went deep four times in the eighth inning of an 8-2 victory over the San Francisco Giants on Friday night.
Max Muncy and Kyle Tucker connected back-to-back in the eighth. Betts and Max Muncy added two-out solo shots in a five-run inning as the NL West champions rolled in a series opener between old rivals.
Tyler Glasnow (5-1) allowed two runs and three hits in six innings with a season-high 10 strikeouts.
The home run barrage occurred on the 20th anniversary of the Dodgers' four-plus-one game. Jeff Kent, J.D. Drew, Russell Martin and Marlon Anderson hit four consecutive homers in the bottom of the ninth inning — the fourth time in major league history the feat had been accomplished.
Giants reliever Philip Abner gave up all five runs in the eighth, which began with the Dodgers leading 3-2. He became the second reliever in Giants history to give up four homers in one inning.
The Giants (64-90) lost their 90th game, their most since 2017 when they dropped 98.
Muncy’s shot traveled 420 feet and Tucker’s went 403 feet, both to right-center. Betts also homered leading off the game.
Josue De Paula, a 21-year-old Dodgers rookie finishing his first week in the major leagues, lined a two-out double to right field for the go-ahead run in the sixth. He also singled and scored the tying run on Teoscar Hernández’s RBI single in the fifth.
Edwin Díaz struck out two in a scoreless ninth in his return from the injured list.
The Giants tied the game at 1 on Jung Hoo Lee's leadoff homer in the second and went ahead 2-1 on Jonah Cox's RBI single with two outs in the third.
Giants starter Cesar Perdomo gave up two runs and six hits in 4 2/3 innings with one strikeout. Jason Foley (3-2) took the loss in relief.
Giants first baseman Bryce Eldridge was a late scratch with a head laceration.
Up next
The Giants had yet to announce a starter for Saturday against Dodgers LHP Tarik Skubal (10-7, 2.70 ERA).

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Dodgers surge late to beat Giants as they work to get healthy for playoffs
item.dc:creator: Kevin Baxter
item.description: Dodgers surge late to beat Giants as they work to get healthy for playoffs - Click here to listen to this article - - Tyler Glasnow gives up three hits, two runs and strikes out 10 over six innings in the Dodgers’ 8-2 win over the San Francisco Giants. - The Dodgers hit four home runs in the eighth inning, including a pair of back-to-back homers. Mookie Betts finished with two home runs. With eight games left in the regular season, the Dodgers have already ticked off the most important box
item.content:encoded:
Dodgers surge late to beat Giants as they work to get healthy for playoffs
- Click here to listen to this article
-
- Tyler Glasnow gives up three hits, two runs and strikes out 10 over six innings in the Dodgers’ 8-2 win over the San Francisco Giants.
- The Dodgers hit four home runs in the eighth inning, including a pair of back-to-back homers. Mookie Betts finished with two home runs.
With eight games left in the regular season, the Dodgers have already ticked off the most important boxes on their postseason to-do list.
They clinched a playoff berth for a record-tying 14th straight season and won the division title for the fifth time in a row. And with Friday’s 8-2 victory over the San Francisco Giants, the Dodgers (94-60) also have an outside shot at their fourth 100-win season in six years.
But that doesn’t mean they don’t have a lot of work to do between now and the start of the playoffs — the most important task being determining exactly where and when they’ll open the postseason.
With Friday’s win and the Milwaukee Brewers’ victory in Baltimore, the Dodgers trail the Brewers by two games in the race for the league’s best record and the home-field advantage in the postseason that goes with it. They also lead the Atlanta Braves by four games for the league’s second-best record, which would give them a first-round playoff bye and an extra five days to get their sizable contingent of walking wounded healthy.
The magic is indeed missing, and after two seasons of conjuring up postseason greatness, these back-to-reality Dodgers appear headed for an early fall.
“To get one of these top two seeds is important. And our guys understand that,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “Winning the division is great, but I still think our best baseball is ahead of us.”
Achieving that, however, will require emptying an injury list that is almost as long as the team’s starting lineup. If the season ended today, the Dodgers would have at least seven players who wouldn’t be ready to play.
The Dodgers are also hopeful left-hander Blake Snell, who came out of Wednesday’s game after an inning with groin tightness, will be healthy enough to return for one more regular-season start.
Center fielder Andy Pages, who shares the team lead in RBIs with Shohei Ohtani despite missing a month with a fracture in his left hand, is expected to be activated for the series against the San Diego Padres, which begins Tuesday, while backup catcher Dalton Rushing is swinging a bat and will hit against a pitching machine this weekend.
Right-hander Roki Sasaki threw 48 pitches in a bullpen session Wednesday and could come off the IL next week but right-hander Edgardo Henriquez, second among Dodger relievers in innings and strikeouts, will miss the rest of the regular season with a back strain. He could join the team for the playoffs.
Then there’s Ohtani, the four-time MVP. He’s dealing with injuries to his left knee and right biceps. He has resumed taking batting practice and is eligible to come off the IL Wednesday. Roberts said he hopes to get Ohtani 10-12 at-bats before the playoffs.
“I’m just really waiting to hear when he’s going to get on the field, let alone take live BP,” Roberts said. “He’s not there yet. But everything I’ve heard, it’s been a really productive last three to four to five days.”
One player who did return was closer Edwin Díaz. Limited by multiple injuries to just 16 appearances this season, he was activated off the injured list Friday and threw 17 pitches in the ninth, giving up a single and striking out two batters.
For Roberts, the last month has looked like an episode of “The Pitt,” with medical crises piling up, one atop the other. Yet that’s hardly slowed the Dodgers, who opened their final homestand of the season having won 11 of their past 14 games.
Now the focus becomes continuing that momentum while getting as close to full strength as possible.
“They can go hand in hand,” Roberts said. “We have a lot of good players that are more than capable of helping us win baseball games, at the same time making sure we try to get our best players to optimum health when the postseason starts.”
The Dodgers got a big lift Friday from rookie Josue De Paula, a player who didn’t figure in their postseason plans until a week ago, when he was called up to take Ohtani’s place. In his Dodger Stadium debut, De Paula singled and scored on a Teoscar Hernández single in the fifth, then roped a double to the wall in right-center an inning later, scoring Kyle Tucker to put the Dodgers ahead to stay.
Tucker, Max Muncy, Mookie Betts and Will Smith all homered in a five-run eighth inning, turning a nail-biter into a comfortable win.
Dodgers owner Mark Walter and multiple insurance companies he owns are being sued for allegedly failing to disclose an ongoing federal probe to customers.
That gave right-hander Tyler Glasnow (5-1) his second win since April 23. Glasnow gave up just three hits in six innings, striking out a season-high 10 batters.
Hernández, who had two hits, is batting .368 with 17 RBIs in September; Tucker, who also had two hits, is hitting .424 with five home runs and 13 runs scored in his past 10 games; while Betts, with two homers Friday, has six hits in his past eight at-bats, lifting his average to a season-high .254.
That’s helped make up for Freddie Freeman’s struggles. Freeman, who went hitless in four at-bats Friday, striking out twice, has just six hits — and 13 strikeouts — in his last 48 at-bats.
“We still have a lot of work to do,” Roberts said before the game.
They have just over a week left to get it done.

item.content:encoded:
Dodgers Closer Edwin Diaz Returns After Missing Month With Neck Injury
Los Angeles Dodgers closer Edwin Diaz came off the injured list Friday after missing a month with a neck injury.
The 32-year-old right-hander was available out of the bullpen for the series opener against San Francisco.
Díaz is 2-2 with an 11.85 ERA in 16 games with the Dodgers. He signed with the team as a free agent last offseason.
He made five rehab appearances during his second IL stint of the season. Díaz allowed six runs and had four strikeouts in 4 1/3 innings.
Right-hander Landon Knack was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City, a day after throwing four scoreless innings in a victory over the Cincinnati Reds.
Reporting by The Associated Press.

item.title: [Orange County Register] Dodgers’ Shohei Ohtani making swing progress on IL
item.dc:creator: Janis Carr
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani casually strolled into the clubhouse on Friday, having received a positive report from his latest batting practice session that has progressed to taking pitches off coaches. “He’s in a good spot,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said before Friday’s opener against the San Francisco Giants. “He hit today and came out of it well. I’m just waiting to hear when he’s going to get on the field or take live BP or Trajekt. “He’s not there yet, but from everything I’
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Dodgers star Shohei Ohtani casually strolled into the clubhouse on Friday, having received a positive report from his latest batting practice session that has progressed to taking pitches off coaches.
“He’s in a good spot,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said before Friday’s opener against the San Francisco Giants. “He hit today and came out of it well. I’m just waiting to hear when he’s going to get on the field or take live BP or Trajekt.
“He’s not there yet, but from everything I’ve heard it’s been a really productive last three to four to five days.”
Ohtani reunited with the team after their seven-game trip culminated with the Dodgers clinching the NL West title for the 13th time in 14 years with a win in Cincinnati on Thursday.
Ohtani, who went on the 15-day injured list just before the trip with right biceps and left knee issues, remained in Los Angeles to receive treatment. The four-time league MVP had been taking swings off a tee for several days before Friday.
He is eligible for activation as soon as Wednesday during the team’s final home series against the San Diego Padres, but when he rejoins the lineup will depend on his progress. Roberts is counting on Ohtani getting a few regular-season games before the postseason begins.
Before that happens, Roberts said he would like to see Ohtani take somewhere between 10 and 12 at-bats before putting him in the lineup.
“I think no matter what I say, it really doesn’t matter in the sense of it’s what he feels good with, what gets him ready,” Roberts said. “So, I could say 10, but it could be 12. But I think for me, if I’m just kind of spit balling and I think that 10 to 12 would be great.”
DIAZ IS ACTIVATED
Relief pitcher Edwin Diaz returned to the bullpen for Friday’s series opener. Roberts has said the 32-year-old right-hander will be used in low-leverage situations after missing a month because of neck inflammation.
Diaz has struggled with injuries (elbow surgery) and underperformance in his first season with the team, going 2-2 with an 11.85 ERA in 16 games with 19 strikeouts and 10 walks over 13⅔ innings. He made five rehab appearances with Triple-A Oklahoma City during his second IL stint of the season, allowing six runs with four strikeouts in 4⅓ innings.
Roberts said he just wants to see Diaz have success on the mound during the nine remaining regular-season games.
“Just pitch,” Roberts said of his expectations for Diaz. “Regardless of the role, I think we just want to see him throw the baseball the way he’s capable of. And you’re talking about nine games, so you’re talking three or four outings to evaluate and that should be adequate.”
To create a roster spot for Diaz, right-hander Landon Knack was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City, a day after throwing four scoreless innings in a victory over the Cincinnati Reds.
HELP ON THE HORIZON
Outfielder Andy Pages is set to return on Tuesday against the Padres after missing a month because of a hand fracture, but the news isn’t as hopeful for backup catcher Dalton Rushing.
Pages got hit by a pitch in a game last month against the Pittsburgh Pirates and subsequently had surgery to place a screw in his fifth metacarpal. He has been steadily increasing his baseball activity.
While Rushing is progressing from right elbow trouble, Roberts didn’t have a date for his return.
Rushing appeared in four games off the bench before going back on the 10-day injured list after missing significant time because of a slight tear in the UCL of his right elbow.
UP NEXT
Giants (TBA) at Dodgers (LHP Tarik Skubal, 10-7, 2.70 ERA), Saturday, 6:10 p.m., SNLA, 570 AM

item.content:encoded:
Denver, Colorado.- El cerrador de los Dodgers, Edwin Díaz, será operado el miércoles en la Clínica Ortopédica Kerlan-Jobe para extraer fragmentos óseos de su codo, según anunció el club antes del partido del lunes contra los Rockies. Díaz, cuyo regreso se espera para la segunda mitad de la temporada, fue colocado en la lista de lesionados el lunes. Como medida complementaria, el club llamó al lanzador zurdo Jake Eder.
Díaz, de 32 años, permitió tres carreras sin conseguir ningún out el domingo contra los Rockies. En lo que va de temporada, tiene marca de 1-0 con una efectividad de 10.50 en siete juegos. El veterano de 10 años tiene una marca de 29-36 en su carrera con una efectividad de 2.91 en 527 juegos. El tres veces All-Star acumula 257 salvamentos en 300 oportunidades con 849 ponches.
“Hoy fue una evaluación difícil”, dijo Roberts después del partido contra Colorado . “Sé cómo debería verse, y cuando no se ve así, me preocupa un poco. Así que hablaré con él”.
La recta de cuatro costuras de Díaz ha promediado entre 97.2 y 99.1 mph en las últimas cuatro temporadas, pero en lo que va de esta temporada solo promedia 95.7 mph, y el domingo en Coors Field llegó a tan solo 92.8 mph. Solo ha lanzado seis rectas más lentas en toda su carrera.
Eder, de 27 años, fue adquirido de los Nationals el 1 de abril a cambio de dinero. Ha participado en tres juegos con el equipo de Triple-A Oklahoma City esta temporada, lanzando 5.1 entradas y permitiendo dos carreras. Lanzó para los Los Angeles Angels en 2025, haciendo ocho apariciones, con un récord de 0-1 y una efectividad de 4.91 en 18.1 entradas.
Hizo su debut en las Grandes Ligas el 17 de septiembre de 2024 como miembro de los Chicago White Sox, permitiendo una carrera en dos entradas. El exjugador de Vanderbilt Commodore fue seleccionado en la cuarta ronda del Draft de Jugadores de Primer Año de 2020 por los Miami Marlins y ha lanzado en 72 juegos de Ligas Menores, con un récord de 10-29, una efectividad de 5.35 y 356 ponches en 312.2 entradas.
Información: MLB.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers injury updates: Where Shohei Ohtani, other stars stand entering final stretch
item.dc:creator: Andrés Soto; USA TODAY
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Dodgers manager Dave Roberts was in good spirits as he sat at the podium beneath Dodger Stadium on Friday, Sept. 18. His team returned home as National League West champions for the 13th time in 14 years after their 8-2 rout of the Cincinnati Reds to end their road trip. They also entered Friday's series opener against the San Francisco Giants with a four-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed in the NL and sat just two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers for the top s
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Dodgers manager Dave Roberts was in good spirits as he sat at the podium beneath Dodger Stadium on Friday, Sept. 18. His team returned home as National League West champions for the 13th time in 14 years after their 8-2 rout of the Cincinnati Reds to end their road trip.
They also entered Friday's series opener against the San Francisco Giants with a four-game lead over the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed in the NL and sat just two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers for the top seed with just nine games to go before October.
But perhaps taking priority over chasing playoff positioning, Roberts expressed confidence that the Dodgers could finish the season relatively healthy with both Shohei Ohtani and Blake Snell progressing well in the final two weeks of the regular season.
"I think it's about winning games, all the while ... getting our players back to health. But I think they can go hand in hand," Roberts said. "We have a lot of good players that are more than capable of helping us win baseball games and at the same time, making sure we try to get our best players to optimum health when the postseason starts."
Ohtani, who has been rehabbing at home while the Dodgers were on the road, swung a bat for the second time since landing on the 15-day injured list on Sept. 8. The two-way superstar took another step forward in his hitting progression as he took batting practice off of coach pitch and came away feeling good, per Roberts. While the Dodgers' skipper acknowledged "he's not there yet" as far as facing live pitching, that would be the next hurdle for Ohtani to clear before returning to the lineup.
In an ideal world, Roberts said he'd like for Ohtani to take somewhere around 10-12 at-bats in live batting practice before he gets activated, but acknowledged that it's really dependent on Ohtani himself.
"It's been a really productive three-to-four-to-five days. He's in a good spot," Roberts said. "No matter what I say, it really doesn't matter in the sense of it's what he feels good with, what gets him ready."
Snell, who exited his last start in Cincinnati after pitching just one inning with left groin tightness, continues to feel good and the overall sense is that he avoided a serious injury. Snell threw 90 feet on Friday while wearing a wrap around his left groin area, and Roberts is "very hopeful" that the former Cy Young winner can make one more regular season start.
Roberts is not sure when exactly that would be but did say that it would be a full start to ramp Snell up for the postseason rather than an abbreviated one.
"It'd be more of a normal start, maybe not pushing him a ton given we don't know how the season's going to play out," Roberts said. "But this will be his last regular season start, so I think it'd be more of a regular start."
The Dodgers' depleted bullpen does get some reinforcements back with closer Edwin Díaz being activated from the IL. He's available to pitch on Friday night if needed, and Roberts didn't rule out using him in low leverage situations to try and get him into a rhythm ahead of October.
Roberts also said that he expects outfielder Andy Pages to be activated at some point in the final home series against the San Diego Padres and catcher Dalton Rushing has also been progressing well, though there's no timeline on his return just yet.
This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Dodgers injury updates: Where Shohei Ohtani, other stars stand entering final stretch

RESUMEN
EL NUEVO DIARIO, LOS ÁNGELES.- El cerrador de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, Edwin Díaz, salió el viernes de la lista de lesionados tras perderse un mes de actividad debido a una lesión en el cuello, según un reporte de MLB.com.
El lanzador derecho de 32 años estuvo disponible en el bullpen para el inicio de la serie contra San Francisco.
Díaz registra una marca de 2-2 y una efectividad de 11.85 en 16 partidos con los Dodgers. Firmó con el equipo como agente libre durante la pasada temporada baja.
Realizó cinco apariciones de rehabilitación durante su segunda estancia en la lista de lesionados esta temporada. Díaz permitió seis carreras y logró cuatro ponches en 4 entradas y un tercio.
El lanzador derecho Landon Knack fue enviado a Triple-A Oklahoma City, un día después de lanzar cuatro entradas en blanco en una victoria sobre los Rojos de Cincinnati.

item.content:encoded:
Díaz podría lanzar entradas de baja presión mientras lucha por un puesto en playoffs
This browser does not support the video element.
LOS ÁNGELES - Los Dodgers firmaron al puertorriqueño Edwin Díaz la temporada baja pasada con la firme intención de que fuera su cerrador para el 2026 y más allá. Ahora que regresa tras su segunda estancia en la lista de lesionados esta temporada, se ve obligado a luchar por un puesto en el bullpen de L.A. para la postemporada.
Antes del inicio de la serie del viernes contra los Gigantes en el Dodger Stadium, los Dodgers activaron a Díaz de la lista de lesionados de 15 días, a la que había ingresado el 18 de agosto debido a una inflamación en el cuello. Como movimiento correspondiente, el lanzador derecho Landon Knack fue enviado a Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Ha sido un año turbulento para Díaz, quien el 12 de diciembre firmó un contrato de tres años y $US69 millones con los bicampeones defensores de la Serie Mundial. Huelga decir que las cosas no han salido según lo previsto para el tres veces seleccionado al Juego de Estrellas. En sus primeras siete presentaciones, permitió siete carreras limpias en seis entradas, con 10 ponches y cinco bases por bolas; posteriormente, ingresó a la lista de lesionados debido a cuerpos libres en el codo derecho que requirieron cirugía.
Tras su regreso el 29 de julio, Díaz retomó el rol de cerrador, aunque esta vez registró tres oportunidades de salvamento desperdiciadas en nueve partidos y acumuló una efectividad de 12.91, con nueve ponches, cinco bases por bolas y dos bateadores golpeados en 7 entradas y 2/3 de labor.
La asignación de rehabilitación más reciente de Díaz no generó mucha confianza. Aunque los resultados eran menos importantes que sus sensaciones físicas, tuvo problemas de control: otorgó siete bases por bolas y golpeó a un bateador en cuatro entradas y 1/3 repartidas en cinco salidas con Oklahoma City, logrando además muy pocos swings fallidos.
Entonces, ¿qué debe hacer Díaz para demostrar que merece formar parte de los planes de L.A. para la postemporada?
"Creo que simplemente lanzar bien", dijo el manager Dave Roberts. "Para mí, el rol no importa. Creo que solo queremos verlo lanzar como él es capaz de hacerlo. Y estamos hablando de nueve partidos [restantes en la temporada regular], así que hablamos de tres o cuatro salidas para evaluar, y eso debería ser suficiente".
En este momento, ese rol no será el de "cerrador". Cabe esperar que Díaz sea utilizado en situaciones de menor presión. Tras asegurar su 13er título de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional en las últimas 14 temporadas —y mientras luchan por obtener el pase directo a la segunda ronda de los playoffs—, los Dodgers tienen el lujo de aprovechar el resto del calendario de la temporada regular para que varios jugadores se ganen, en la práctica, un puesto en el roster de octubre.
Díaz podría ser la figura más destacada de ese grupo. Este tres veces ganador del premio al Relevista del Año podría convertirse en un factor clave en el bullpen de Los Ángeles en su búsqueda de un tercer título consecutivo, siempre y cuando demuestre ser una opción viable.

item.title: [MLB.com] Díaz likely to pitch low-leverage innings as he vies for postseason spot
item.dc:creator: Sarah Wexler
item.description: LOS ANGELES -- The Dodgers signed Edwin Díaz last offseason with every intention of him being their closer, for 2026 and beyond. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES -- The Dodgers signed Edwin Díaz last offseason with every intention of him being their closer, for 2026 and beyond. As he returns from his second injured list stint this season, he finds himself needing to fight for a role in L.A.’s postseason bullpen.
Prior to Friday’s series opener against the Giants at Dodger Stadium, the Dodgers activated Díaz from the 15-day IL, where he’d landed on Aug. 18 with neck inflammation. Right-hander Landon Knack was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City as the corresponding move.
It’s been a tumultuous year for Díaz, who on Dec. 12 signed a three-year, $69 million contract with the two-time reigning World Series champs. Needless to say, things have not gone as expected for the three-time All-Star. Across his first seven appearances, he allowed seven earned runs in six innings with 10 strikeouts and five walks, after which he landed on the IL with loose bodies in his right elbow that necessitated surgery.
Upon his return on July 29, Díaz slotted back into the closer role, this time recording three blown saves over nine games and pitching to a 12.91 ERA, with nine strikeouts, five walks and two hit batters in 7 2/3 innings pitched.
Díaz’s most recent rehab assignment didn’t do much to inspire confidence. Although the results were less important than how he came out feeling, he struggled with his command, issuing seven walks and hitting a batter in 4 1/3 innings across five appearances with Oklahoma City while recording very few swings and misses.
So what does Díaz have to do to prove he deserves to be part of L.A.’s postseason plans?
“I think just pitch well,” said manager Dave Roberts. “For me, it's regardless of the role. I think we just want to see him throw the baseball the way he's capable of. And you're talking about nine games [remaining in the regular season], so you're talking three or four outings to evaluate, and that should be adequate.”
At this point, that role will not be “closer.” Expect to see Díaz used in lower-leverage spots. With their 13th National League West title in the last 14 seasons now clinched -- even as they vie for a first-round bye -- the Dodgers have the luxury of being able to use their remaining regular-season slate to let a handful of guys essentially try out for October roster spots.
Díaz might just be the headliner of that group, as the three-time Reliever of the Year could prove to be an X-factor out of L.A.’s ’pen as it seeks a three-peat -- so long as he shows he’s a viable option.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers have officially activated Edwin Diaz from the injured list and optioned reliever Landon Knack back down to the minor leagues.
Diaz has been rehabilitating down in Triple-A with the Oklahoma City Comets as he tries to recover from neck inflammation.
In 4.1 innings of work in the minors during his latest assignment, he has a 12.46 ERA.
With the season winding down for the Comets and Diaz still needing to pitch and prove that he can get outs, the Dodgers are giving him a shot on the major league roster.
Manager Dave Roberts has made it clear that Diaz needs to show tangible results in the regular season to get any standing in the bullpen trust tree.
“We have to go with our best pitchers, as far as performance, talent, all that stuff,” Roberts said.
“So my bet is that he will be (on the roster). But again, there’s got to be some kind of evidence or something for us, again, to sort of bet on. And so my bet is yes, but we still got to see something.”
This story will be updated.

In 16 appearances with the Dodgers this season, Díaz has
item.content:encoded:
The Dodgers on Friday activated Edwin Díaz off the injured list, with a week and a half remaining in the regular season to see if his slim chance of pitching his way onto the postseason roster comes to fruition.
Díaz, who signed a three-year contract with the Dodgers in December, struggled to open the season before undergoing arthroscopic surgery to remove loose bodies from his right elbow in April, which cost him three and a half months.
In 16 appearances with the Dodgers this season, Díaz has allowed runs in nine of them, with an 11.85 ERA, 6.37 xERA, 19 strikeouts and 10 walks in 13 2/3 innings. In nine games after returning from elbow surgery, Díaz had a 19.6-percent strikeout rate, down from 30.3 percent in seven games before surgery, and well below his 39.9-percent career strikeout rate through 2025.
The latest malady for Díaz was neck inflammation, sidelined since August 18. His rehab assignment with Oklahoma City didn't go well at all, throwing more balls than strikes in three of his five appearances, with six runs allowed in 4 1/3 innings, seven walks, and four strikeouts. Manager Dave Roberts told reporters on Thursday in Cincinnati that Díaz will need to throw more strikes, and quality ones at that, in order to be considered to pitch in October.
"Like anything, it should be a meritocracy. You have to earn the right of opportunities, and you've also got to perform. Eddie understands that," Roberts said, as shown on SportsNet LA. "Where we're at now, we need guys to buy in, perform and go from there. That's what he's about."
Landon Knack was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City, after fulfilling his role with aplomb on Thursday. Called up for a day, Knack tossed four scoreless innings in relief and earned the win in the Dodgers' division clincher in Cincinnati.
In Knack's three stints in the majors this year, he pitched in four of the eight games for which he was active, with a 3.86 ERA and 4.09 xERA in build relief, with eight strikeouts and two walks in his 11 2/3 innings, plus one save of 2 2/3 innings, the Dodgers' longest save of the season.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are giving Edwin Díaz one final chance to prove he belongs on the postseason roster.
On Friday, ahead of their series opener against the San Francisco Giants, the Dodgers have officially activated Díaz off the 15-day injured list. In order to make room on the active roster, right-hander Landon Knack was optioned.
Díaz joined the Dodgers this offseason on a three-year, $69 million deal to be the team's closer. He had a 10.50 ERA over six innings before going on the injured list and undergoing surgery to remove loose bodies in his elbow.
Díaz made his long-awaited return in late July, and the Dodgers were hoping his early-season issues would be behind him.
Unfortunately, that wasn't the case.
The three-time All-Star had an even worse 12.91 ERA over 7.2 innings. He then went back on the IL — this time with a neck injury — and has been out for the last month.
Díaz struggled on his rehab assignment, and there were questions about whether the team would even give him another chance this season.
“He needs to pitch better. It hasn’t been good,” manager Dave Roberts said on Monday. “He’s going to pitch on Wednesday, and I guess we’ll evaluate then. I think the world of him. The baseball card looks great. But where we’re at, there’s got to be something for us to be able to hang our hat on. And he knows that. He knows that. He wants to pitch well."
He had a better rehab outing on Wednesday, pitching one scoreless inning. That was enough for the Dodgers to give him one more opportunity at the big league level.
It won't be as the team's closer, though.
What Will Edwin Diaz's Role Be For Dodgers?
The Dodgers will be using Díaz in low-leverage spots at first as they see if he can be an option for the postseason roster.
“I think like anything, it should be a meritocracy,” Roberts said. “You have to earn the right of opportunities, but then you also got to perform, right? Eddie understands that. I think where we’re at now, we just need guys to buy in, perform and go from there. That’s what he’s about.”
Across Díaz's 16 appearances this season, he has a disastrous 11.85 ERA and four blown saves in 11 chances.
However, if he returns to form in time for the playoffs, all will be forgotten from his disappointing first season in LA.
Sign up for our free newsletter and follow us on X/Twitter and Facebook for the latest news.
Noah Camras graduated from the University of Southern California in 2022 with a B.A. in Journalism and a minor in sports media studies. He was born and raised in Los Angeles and has extensively covered Southern California sports in his career. Noah is the publisher of Dodgers on SI after contributing as a writer and editor over the last three years.

item.content:encoded:
Mookie Betts: “Nos queda un largo camino por recorrer”
El campocorto de los Dodgers coloca en perspectiva la participación de la novena en la postemporada por decimotercera vez en los últimos 14 años.
PUBLICIDAD
Cincinnati. Los Dodgers de Los Ángeles aseguraron su quinto título consecutivo de la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional y el 13ro en las últimas 14 temporadas al vencer el jueves 8-2 a los Reds de Cincinnati.
“Es algo muy importante. Creo que mucha gente piensa que es solo un rito de paso (pero) no es fácil”, declaró el mánager de los Dodgers Dave Roberts. “Así que es algo de lo que todos estamos muy orgullosos, pero entendemos claramente que ese no es el objetivo final”.
Los Dodgers (93-60) disputarán los playoffs por 14 temporada consecutiva, con lo que igualan el récord que los Bravos de Atlanta establecieron de 1991-2005.
Sights and sounds from the clubhouse. 👀 pic.twitter.com/0UTzHdvvpK
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) September 18, 2026
“Es el primer paso”, dijo Mookie Betts mientras se secaba el champán de los ojos. “Nos queda un largo camino por recorrer”.
La celebración en el terreno de juego fue algo calmada tras el último out el jueves. Pero los jugadores se soltaron en el vestuario, donde el champán y la cerveza salpicaron desde el suelo hasta el techo.
“Creo que es una de esas situaciones en las que, como en el béisbol se juega a diario, los jugadores se centran en rendir”, dijo Roberts. “Así que no hay muchos momentos para celebrar. Por eso es agradable ver a los chicos soltarse un poco”.
A pesar de todos sus laureles, los Dodgers creen que todavía tienen algo que demostrar.
El año pasado, el equipo pulverizó el récord de gasto de las Grandes Ligas con una nómina total de 515 millones de dólares, dando alas a críticas de que tienen una supuesta ventaja injusta.
“Lo que estamos creando aquí es especial”, afirmó Max Muncy. “Definitivamente no se le da el reconocimiento que merece. Todo el mundo se fija en la nómina, pero nunca hablamos de cómo hacemos las cosas bien, de cómo nos preparamos adecuadamente o de cómo cuidamos todos esos pequeños detalles. De eso no se habla”.
Doc and the boys are ready for October. pic.twitter.com/krnwXYR7ap
— Los Angeles Dodgers (@Dodgers) September 17, 2026
Los bicampeones defensores de la Serie Mundial aún pujan por el primer puesto de preclasificación de la Liga Nacional, que actualmente está en posesión de los Cerveceros de Milwaukee. Los Ángeles comenzó el día con una ventaja de tres juegos y medio sobre los Bravos (89-64) por el segundo puesto, pero está por detrás de los Cerveceros (95-57).
“Seguimos luchando por uno de los dos primeros puestos”, dijo Roberts. “Creo que hacemos bien celebrando, pero sin dejar que eso afecte a lo que sigue. Tenemos que tomar el vuelo y jugar contra los Gigantes mañana”.
Los Dodgers buscan convertirse en el primer equipo en conquistar tres campeonatos consecutivos de la Serie Mundial desde que los Yankees lo lograron de 1998 a 2000.
Este es el cuarto título divisional asegurado más temprano para los Dodgers. Aseguraron el Oeste de la Liga Nacional el 10 de septiembre de 2019, el 13 de septiembre de 2022 y el 16 de septiembre de 2023.
Los Ángeles aprovechará ese tiempo para recuperar lesionados. Eso empieza con Shohei Ohtani.
El cuatro veces Jugador Más Valioso ha estado en la lista de lesionados de 15 días desde el 8 de septiembre por una inflamación en el bíceps derecho y les dijo a los reporteros a principios de este mes que ya no lanzará más en lo que resta de temporada. La estrella de dos vías hizo swings desde un tee por primera vez el martes y se sintió bien. Se espera que regrese como bateador antes de que termine la temporada regular, aunque no está claro si podrá llegar al 100% de salud antes de octubre.
Roki Sasaki, en la lista de lesionados por una ampolla en el dedo medio, lanzó en una práctica de bateo en vivo el miércoles en Cincinnati y salió bien. Roberts indicó que su próxima aparición será como abridor.
Blake Snell salió prematuramente de la apertura del miércoles después de un inning por rigidez en la ingle izquierda. Su situación es incierta.
Se espera que el cerrador puertorriqueño Edwin Díaz, quien ha estado en la lista de lesionados desde agosto por una inflamación en el cuello, sea activado el viernes. El venezolano Edgardo Henríquez, un preparador de mesa en el bullpeb, está en la lista de lesionados por molestias en la parte baja de la espalda. Se le realizó una resonancia magnética en Los Ángeles el miércoles, que reveló una distensión lumbar, y su rehabilitación se pausará por unos días.
El primera base Freddie Freeman, aquejado por dolor en la rodilla derecha, regresó a la alineación el martes y cortó una mala racha de 3 hits en 30 turnos con tres imparables. Sumó otros dos hits el jueves.
Los Dodgers protagonizaron el mayor impacto de la fecha límite de cambios al adquirir a Tarik Skubal, ganador en dos ocasiones del premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana, procedente de los Tigres. Skubal tiene marca de 3-2 con efectividad de 2.52 en ocho aperturas con los Dodgers.
La incorporación de Skubal convirtió a los Dodgers en los grandes favoritos en las apuestas para ganar la Serie Mundial. Pero después de comenzar la temporada con marca de 61-36, los Dodgers tienen registro de 31-24 desde la pausa del Juego de Estrellas.
Los Dodgers dejaron a 12 corredores en base y se fueron de 0 en 11 con corredores en posición de anotar en la derrota del miércoles ante los Reds, algo que, según Roberts, necesita mejorar.
“Se trata de poder rematar a los equipos cuando tenemos oportunidades. En la postemporada no se presentan muchas oportunidades. Hay que saber aprovecharlas”, dijo Roberts.
___
