item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers had yet another dream offseason in 2025-26.
The Dodgers were once again viewed as the winners of the offseason, earning the honor among media and fans for the third straight year after signing closer Edwin Diaz and star outfielder Kyle Tucker.
Diaz and Tucker signed lucrative contracts with the Dodgers; however, neither has panned out anywhere close to where the Dodgers had hoped.
Instead, ESPN's Bradford Doolittle labeled the two as the biggest disappointment for the Dodgers as the regular season winds down.
"The Dodgers' splash signings of Tucker and Edwin Diaz in last season's free agency were the cause of much handwringing about LA's economic dominance," Doolittle wrote.
"While those high-level, targeted acquisitions looked like no-brainers at the time, the first year of both deals could hardly have gone worse. Together, Tucker and Diaz are at minus-1.0 bWAR for their Dodgers debuts while earning a combined $47 million. Ouch."
How Has Edwin Diaz Been for the Dodgers?
Diaz was the first of the two to sign, inking a three-year, $69 million contract with the Dodgers.
The Dodgers made him the highest-paid closer by average annual salary, and as the season winds down, that contract is looking like an utter disaster. In 16 appearances this year, Diaz has posted a 11.85 ERA, 2.56 WHIP and 19 strikeouts in 13.2 innings.
The 32-year-old has blown four saves out of 11 opportunities. On top of that, batters are hitting a staggering .385 against him in Los Angeles.
Diaz has also struggled with injuries. He's missed significant time due to elbow surgery and is currently on the injured list with neck inflammation.
His lack of results, inconsistencies and injuries have cast serious doubt on whether he will even make the Dodgers' postseason roster.
How Has Kyle Tucker Been for the Dodgers?
As for Tucker, he's been available, but just hasn't performed.
The Dodgers signed the 29-year-old to a lucrative deal, carrying the highest present-day average annual value (AAV) in MLB history at $57.1 million per year.
However, Tucker hasn't performed at that level for most of the season.
The overall numbers alone are worrisome. Tucker is batting .226 with 15 home runs, 66 RBIs, 11 stolen bases and 113 hits in 500 at-bats. His OPS is just .701.
Tucker will continue to get everyday opportunities through the end of the regular season and the posteason. If he can play well in October, all will be forgotten from his disappointing first year.
Sign up for our free newsletter and follow us on X/Twitter and Facebook for the latest news.
Ricardo Sandoval is a freelance writer with On SI. He is a graduate of California State University, Northridge, and specializes in sports writing, particularly in MLB, NBA and NFL. He previously served as an Associate Editor for Dodgers Nation and has worked with Newsweek and The Sporting News.
Follow @_RicardoSand

item.description: Edwin Diaz signed a three-year, $69 million contract in December. It made him baseball's highest-paid reliever by average annual salary. item.content:encoded:
Edwin Diaz signed a three-year, $69 million contract in December. It made him baseball's highest-paid reliever by average annual salary. His first season for the Los Angeles Dodgers has not matched that price tag.
Diaz opened the year on a rocky note. He allowed one run through his first five outings. Two rough appearances followed.
Doctors then found loose bodies in his right elbow. He had arthroscopic surgery and missed roughly 100 days.
He returned in late July and posted mixed results. The Dodgers placed him back on the injured list Aug. 18. This time, doctors diagnosed inflammation on the right side of his neck.
Diaz has an 11.85 ERA in 16 appearances this season. He has thrown 13 2/3 innings for the Los Angeles Dodgers. The right-hander has struck out 19 batters and walked 10.
That uneven form has created real uncertainty about his spot on the postseason roster.
Edwin Diaz's Roster Spot Now in Doubt
insider Ken Rosenthal addressed Diaz's situation on the show "Foul Territory." He said the Dodgers will pick their 26 best players, regardless of salary.
The club has called this year's pitching staff its deepest ever heading into October.
Rosenthal added that if evaluators view Diaz as not good enough, the Dodgers will leave him off. Rosenthal called it a "win-at-all-costs kind of industry."
Manager Dave Roberts has not guaranteed Diaz a spot either. "We have to go with our best pitchers," Roberts said. Diaz has not pitched well enough yet during his rehab assignment.
He allowed five runs while recording two outs in his Sept. 13 outing. He is set for another rehab appearance Sept. 16, with an expected return in late September.
The stakes are real. The Dodgers clinched a playoff berth Monday with a win over the Cincinnati Reds.
Latest Updates on Edwin Diaz, Shohei Ohtani
The Dodgers updated their injury report this week. Several key players remain sidelined heading into the stretch run.
Diaz remains on the 15-day injured list with neck inflammation. He is on a rehab assignment with Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Shohei Ohtani is on the 15-day injured list with a left knee and right biceps injury, retroactive to Sept. 8. He could return as a hitter as soon as Sept. 23. He is not expected to pitch again until 2027. He began a swing progression Sept. 15, hitting off a tee.
Outfielder Andy Pages has a fractured left hand. He landed on the 10-day injured list Aug. 22. He has progressed to hitting baseballs off a machine, with an expected return in late September as well.

item.title: [Friars on Base] Padres hoping Edwin Díaz makes Dodgers' playoff roster as struggles reach breaking point
item.dc:creator: PJ Potter
item.description: It has been a nightmare season for three-time Reliever of the Year Edwin Díaz. In his first year with the Los Angeles Dodgers, he's made two trips to the injured list, all while logging a -1.3 bWAR and 11.85 ERA. The Dodgers were hoping that Díaz would help cement a third straight World Series title, but considering every bit of struggle from the 32-year-old closer, they may keep him off the postseason roster if no sign of progress is being made. “We have to go with our best pitchers, as far as
item.content:encoded:
It has been a nightmare season for three-time Reliever of the Year Edwin Díaz. In his first year with the Los Angeles Dodgers, he's made two trips to the injured list, all while logging a -1.3 bWAR and 11.85 ERA.
The Dodgers were hoping that Díaz would help cement a third straight World Series title, but considering every bit of struggle from the 32-year-old closer, they may keep him off the postseason roster if no sign of progress is being made.
“We have to go with our best pitchers, as far as performance, talent, all that stuff,” Roberts said in The Athletic's report. “So my bet is that he will be (on the roster). But again, there’s got to be some kind of evidence or something for us, again, to sort of bet on. And so my bet is yes, but we still got to see something.”
The San Diego Padres, among every other National League postseason hopeful, are crossing their fingers that the Dodgers ultimately keep Díaz on the roster.
Padres fans can finally point to a Dodgers' problem with merit
For the last few seasons, it felt like the Dodgers were invincible. Seemingly every MVP and All-Star joined the organization, conjuring up a super team that has baseball fans worried about a potential lockout this upcoming offseason.
So for once, San Diego fans can actually look at Los Angeles and smile as they hold an advantage over them. The Padres have a much better closer, and it's not even close to being an argument anymore.
Mason Miller's 1.12 ERA, 0.855 WHIP, and league-best 37 saves make the Padres that much better of a contending playoff team. The Dodgers can't say about their closer anymore. In a rehab stint this past Sunday with Triple-A Oklahoma City, Díaz was torched for five runs in 0.2 innings against minor leaguers, surrendering three walks and two hits.
Entering Tuesday's games, the Padres would face the Dodgers in the NLDS if they were to advance out of the Wild Card round. The Friars, and their fans, are hoping that Dodgers feel forced to have Díaz on the postseason roster.
After all, he is getting paid $60 million by Los Angeles over the next three seasons. He's not the easiest guy to part with.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers recently sent Edwin Díaz on his second rehab assignment of the season. His first stint in Oklahoma City — back when he was rehabbing following elbow surgery — didn't go well. He posted a 10.80 ERA in just 1⅓ innings. Impossibly, however, he's been even worse his second time around.
Díaz has made four rehab outings for the so far. His first was almost spotless (he gave up a walk), but his second lasted just ⅔ innings after he gave up a run on two walks. The third was a promising bounce back — one hit, one walk, no earned runs in a full inning — but his latest was a downright disaster.
On Sunday, Diaz gave up five earned runs on two hits, a hit by pitch, and three walks. He was yanked before he could get out of the inning.
The Dodgers still have a few days before they need to make a roster move, but under no circumstances can he be used in close games, not even if they clinch a postseason berth. The Atlanta Braves are still within striking distance for a first-round bye, and the Dodgers can't afford to lose it.
When Díaz comes back, the only acceptable situation to use him in would be a blowout, and even then, fans would find it impossible to trust him. Although Tanner Scott appears to be turning back into a pumpkin, even he would lend the team greater reassurances in close games.
Edwin Díaz's latest rehab meltdown should force Dodgers to leave him off their postseason roster
It also puts the Dodgers in an uncomfortable but undeniable position: Díaz can't be on the postseason roster.
Roki Sasaki is likely to go back to the rotation when he returns from injury, but repeating his role as LA's lights-out postseason closer could be on the docket if Scott fails to prove himself trustworthy. Tyler Glasnow is also expected to move to the bullpen in October, so the Dodgers could even audition him in the role.
While the Dodgers are still the heavy favorites to win the World Series, it'll be an undeniable embarrassment to the team if they do it without Díaz — their $69 million man — who they haven't been able to figure out all season long.

item.content:encoded:
How Teoscar Hernández fixed his swing to help power Dodgers over the Reds
- Click here to listen to this article
-
CINCINNATI — A simple change opened a dramatic offensive turnaround for Dodgers left fielder Teoscar Hernández.
Hernández’s two-run homer Tuesday, in the Dodgers’ 4-0 win against the Reds, was his second home run in as many nights, as the team trimmed its magic number to clinch the division to one behind Yoshinobu Yamamoto’s seven innings of one-hit ball. And, significantly, this one was against a right-handed pitcher.
“It’s been very helpful,” manager Dave Roberts said after the game. “As certain guys are not seeing the ball as well, it’s nice to kind of backfill with guys like Teo swinging the bat. And when you can slug like he can, you can win baseball games, and he can carry us for a while. And the last 10 days, something like that, it’s been really good from him.”
Through the end of August, Hernández had just a .668 OPS against right-handed pitchers this season. So, when Roberts was asked in Detroit whether the Dodgers would consider setting up a left-field platoon with the team’s September call-ups, he said yes.
Hernández homered off Tigers left-hander Framber Valdez on the last day of the series. And before the Dodgers opened a three-game set against the Cardinals at Dodger Stadium, Hernández met with the hitting coaches.
Against Valdez, Hernández was in a closed stance, to delay his front hip from opening, according to Dodgers hitting coach Aaron Bates. But the team’s hitting group thought a return to a familiar setup could be a long-term solution.
“It was a great meeting we had,” Bates said. “We all talked about it, and then he felt comfortable enough to do it, and then the rest is to his credit. He’s just been who he is.”
Edwin Díaz struggled in his rehab start Sunday, and Dave Roberts is making it clear the Dodgers “got to see something” before putting him on the playoff roster.
In the past, Hernández had used a “twister tap” as his stride. He started in a more open stance, tapped his toe in line with the pitcher, and then set his foot down. But lower-body injuries the last couple of years — a left groin strain last season and a left hamstring strain earlier this season — forced him away from it.
His improved health and hip flexibility opened the avenue for him to return to that timing mechanism.
“When Teo’s hips are loose that way, and his front leg looks like an Elvis knee, it’s a good sign for us,” Bates said. “Because that means that he can open and close it without his upper body going with it.”
The advantage of the twister tap, as Hernández explained it, is how repeatable it is. A more traditional stride can be sped up or slowed down.
“Just being able to control my body and being in a good position,” Hernández said earlier this month. “I can see the pitch a little sooner and identify what kind of pitch it is and if it’s going to be a strike or a ball.”
With that change, he’s rewarded the Dodgers for deciding against platooning left field. Hernández entered Tuesday with a .777 OPS against right-handed pitchers — a sample size of just 28 plate appearances but still a significant jump.
“The biggest thing is his plate coverage away,” Bates said. “Because now he can spoil pitches, and he’s staying in at-bats longer.”
Hernández’s dramatic offensive turnaround, along with fellow corner outfielder Kyle Tucker’s improvement, have helped steady a Dodgers offense that’s missing Shohei Ohtani (on the IL with right biceps and left knee injuries) and includes a hobbled Freddie Freeman (right knee soreness).
Rookie Josue De Paula, mostly filling in for Ohtani at designated hitter, has already shown he can take mature at-bats and provide some pop. But he’s still finding his footing in a new league.
It lengthens the Dodgers lineup for Hernández, after a slow start to his year, to return to being a veteran power threat — just in time to, ideally, carry the momentum into the postseason.
On Monday, he launched his two-run shot off left-hander Nick Lodolo. On Tuesday, he replicated the feat off right-hander Rhett Lowder.
On the second pitch of the at-bat, Hernández recognized a hung slider, and he roped it over the left-field fence at 109.3 mph, according to Statcast. The blast put the Dodgers up 3-0 in the third inning, with Dodgers starter Yamamoto settling into a groove on the other side.
Yamamoto had walked the first two batters he faced, but he reined in his control to pitch seven scoreless innings and allow just one more baserunner — a double by Reds star shortstop Elly De La Cruz.
The Dodgers also scored on Hunter Feduccia’s second-inning single and Alex Freeland’s seventh-inning homer. And the Dodgers bullpen completed the shutout.
Freeman staying in the lineup
Freeman was all smiles after his three-hit game Tuesday — after going hitless for his last four games.
“I was supposed to be off tomorrow, but I played myself in there,” he said. “So I’m very excited.”
Roberts explained: “He was joking, saying, ‘If I get three hits, then can I be in there tomorrow?’”
Sure enough, the mechanical adjustments he made in the batting cage — focusing on getting his foot down early and making contact out in front — got him there.
“I’m just trying to find something that gives me results,” Freeman said. “We’re at the time where we’re just trying to get hot for five weeks here. So kind of like I did in the World Series a couple years ago, I did the step-out move. That’s not sustainable over six months. I’m not trying to find something that’s sustainable.”
Though Roberts has been trying to find opportunities to rest Freeman, he saw promising signs Tuesday beyond the results.
“Just my eyes, just watching him move, I feel good about him going tomorrow,” Roberts said.
De Paula, Freeland and third baseman Max Muncy will be out of the lineup Wednesday, Roberts said.

item.content:encoded:
Edwin Díaz deberá ganarse la confianza de Dave Roberts para lanzar con los Dodgers en la postemporada
El dirigente de Los Ángeles puso en duda la participación del relevista tras un primer año complicado con los bicampeones.
PUBLICIDAD
El cerrador puertorriqueño Edwin “Sugar” Díaz deberá ganarse su espacio en el roster de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles para poder treparse al montículo durante la postemporada, informó el mánager Dave Roberts en un aparte con la prensa estadounidense.
Díaz ha tenido un primer año complicado tras firmar un contrato de tres campañas y $69 millones con los Dodgers en la temporada muerta. Posee marca de 2-2, siete salvamentos, una errática efectividad de 11.85 en 13.2 entradas lanzadas durante 16 apariciones y ha desperdiciado cuatro de sus 11 oportunidades de salvamento.
También ha permitido 18 carreras, tres de ellas en el noveno inning de su última presentación frente a los Rockies de Colorado el pasado 17 de agosto. Al día siguiente entró a la lista de lesionados por una inflamación en el cuello.
Actualmente se encuentra en una asignación de rehabilitación con los Comets de Oklahoma City, filial de los Dodgers en Triple A. Sin embargo, lo que apuntaba a ser una corta estadía en las Menores para recuperar su nivel ha generado aún más interrogantes sobre el naguabeño, quien hace unos años era considerado uno de los mejores relevistas de las Mayores.
Díaz cargó el domingo con la más reciente derrota de Oklahoma City al permitir cinco carreras y conceder tres bases por bolas ante los Space Cowboys, filial de los Astros de Houston. El derecho pudo retirar a un solo bateador.
Por actuaciones como esas, Roberts entiende que el boricua aún no ha recuperado su nivel y evitó comprometerse cuando la prensa le preguntó si estará entre los lanzadores seleccionados para la postemporada.
Dave Roberts on Edwin Diaz's rehab assignment, via @SonjaMChen:
"He needs to pitch better. It hasn't been good."
Diaz rehab assignment so far:
3.1 IP, 6 ER, 4 K, 3 H, 7 BB pic.twitter.com/304XoBbDsU
“Necesita lanzar mejor. No lo ha hecho bien. Lanzará el miércoles y supongo que lo evaluaremos entonces”, dijo el dirigente de los Dodgers.
“Lo tengo en muy alta estima, pero en esta situación tiene que haber algo que nos dé motivos para estar seguros y él lo sabe. Quiere lanzar bien. Así que, por mi parte, el miércoles lo observaremos con atención”, abundó.
Díaz subirá a la loma el miércoles contra los Chihuahuas de El Paso, filial de los Padres de San Diego en las Menores. La llegada del tres veces seleccionado al Juego de Estrellas a Los Ángeles generó grandes expectativas, ya que era visto como el relevista que le daría a Roberts la seguridad que no tuvo su bullpen en campañas anteriores.
En cambio, el primer año del naguabeño vistiendo el uniforme de Los Ángeles ha estado marcado por lesiones, incluida una en el codo derecho que requirió una intervención quirúrgica y que lo mantuvo fuera por más de tres meses. Aun así, el piloto de los bicampeones continúa apostando en Díaz.
“Tenemos que ir con nuestros mejores lanzadores en términos de rendimiento, talento y todo eso”, indicó Roberts.
“Mi apuesta es que (Díaz) estará (incluido en el roster), pero, nuevamente, tiene que haber algún tipo de evidencia o algo que nos permita confiar en él. Mi apuesta es que sí, pero todavía tenemos que ver algo”, continuó.
Los Dodgers clasificaron el lunes a la postemporada con una victoria sobre los Reds de Cincinnati. Será su decimocuarta aparición consecutiva en los playoffs, empatando así el récord de las Grandes Ligas que los Braves de Atlanta establecieron entre 1991 y 2005. Además, lideran la División Oeste de la Liga Nacional con marca de 91-59.

item.title: [marca usa] Los Dodgers enfrentan una pesadilla con Edwin Díaz rumbo a los playoffs
item.dc:creator: Jose Rodriguez

item.content:encoded:
- MLB. Reaparecen viejos 'fantasmas' para Oneil Cruz por el accidente de tráfico en el que mató a tres personas
- MLB. Drama en Yankee Stadium: Aaron Boone saca a Aaron Judge antes de tiempo en su regreso ante los Rockies
Edwin Díaz pasó de ser una de las grandes apuestas de los Los Angeles Dodgers a convertirse en una de las mayores incógnitas del equipo rumbo a la postemporada. A pesar de firmar un contrato de 69 millones de dólares antes de la temporada 2026, el veterano cerrador podría quedar fuera del roster de playoffs, lo que sería mucho más que una simple decepción.
La prioridad de la organización es clara: llegar a octubre con sus 26 mejores jugadores disponibles, sin importar el salario o la reputación. Y el panorama actual de Díaz no es alentador. Las lesiones lo han limitado a apenas 16 apariciones, mientras que registra una preocupante efectividad de 11.85, muy lejos del nivel que los Dodgers esperaban tras otorgarle uno de los contratos más importantes para un relevista.
Dodgers no garantizan un lugar para Edwin Díaz en playoffs
El reconocido analista de MLB Ken Rosenthal reveló que los Dodgers están considerando seriamente dejar fuera al relevista puertorriqueño del roster de postemporada si no demuestra que puede ser una de sus mejores opciones en el bullpen.
“Si eres los Dodgers, vas a llevar a tus 26 mejores jugadores. Han hablado en distintos momentos sobre cómo sienten que este año su cuerpo de lanzadores, del uno al 13 o del uno al 12 en la postemporada, podría ser el más fuerte que hayan llevado a octubre”, explicó Rosenthal durante una aparición en Foul Territory.
El periodista resumió todavía más la filosofía de la organización angelina:
“Esta es una industria donde se gana a cualquier costo”.
La posibilidad de que un cerrador tres veces All-Star y uno de los relevistas mejor pagados de las Grandes Ligas quede fuera del roster de playoffs habría parecido impensable hace apenas unos meses. Sin embargo, las lesiones y su bajo rendimiento han cambiado por completo el panorama.
Aun así, la puerta no está cerrada. Rosenthal considera que Díaz todavía tiene tiempo para recuperar su mejor versión y convencer a los Dodgers de que merece un lugar en el roster de octubre.
Por ahora, Los Ángeles mantiene abiertas todas sus opciones en una decisión que podría convertirse en una de las historias más sorprendentes de la recta final de la temporada.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Edgardo Henriquez injury just flipped the Dodgers' season upside down

Henriquez has been placed on the 15-day IL, but there remains a path for him returning during the playoffs if all goes well. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are in familiar territory with the playoffs less than two weeks away. They are once again looking for answers in their bullpen. The Dodgers have placed Edgardo Henriquez on the IL with lower back discomfort, and he has been ruled out for the remainder of the regular season.
Henriquez has been placed on the 15-day IL, but there remains a path for him returning during the playoffs if all goes well. While the Dodgers made Edwin Diaz a priority this past offseason, it has been Henriquez who has kept the bullpen together.
Through 61 appearances, Henriquez had a 2.85 ERA while striking out over 29% of the hitters he's faced. If he's unable to return to LA's bullpen during the playoffs, the unit is suddenly facing a problem.
Edgardo Henriquez injury leaves Dodgers facing reality they desperately wanted to avoid
While the Dodgers have a healthy amount of left-handed options in the bullpen — considering Tanner Scott once again becoming an effective option at the end of games — as well as Alex Vesia and Jack Dreyer, they don't really have an established option among righties.
Brock Stewart hasn't looked bad this season, but injuries have limited him to just 22 innings pitched this season. Evan Phillips is back in the bullpen, and while he has 3.68 ERA through 27 appearances, his FIP of 4.65 makes him a regression candidate ahead of the playoffs.
It also doesn't help matters that the Dodgers aren't viewing the return of Diaz as a potential solution. He is currently on a minor-league rehab assignment, but the results simply haven't been there. It's forced Dave Roberts to offer a blunt assessment on Diaz earlier this week, suggesting there's a chance he's left off the playoff roster if he can't overcome his current struggles.
That is why Henriquez's injury is such a blow. He was a clear answer for what the Dodgers lacked in the bullpen, and coupling that with Diaz's struggles, Roberts and Co. are back at the drawing board. Perhaps Kris Bubic could be an answer. Bubic is with the Dodgers after a successful rehab assignment earlier this month and is expected to be reinstated from the IL in the coming days.
If there is a silver lining for the Dodgers, outside of Shohei Ohtani, their starting rotation is healthy and that could ultimately prove to be the difference-maker during the playoffs.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers made Edwin Diaz the highest paid closer over the offseason. Now, he might not even make the postseason roster.
Diaz had a rehab outing Sunday in which he faced eight batters, retiring only two while walking three and hitting a batter. He threw 30 pitches to get those two outs, with only 13 strikes. Manager Dave Roberts talked about his recent woes on Monday before the Dodgers game against the Cincinnati Reds.
“He needs to pitch better. It hasn’t been good,” Roberts said on Monday. “He’s going to pitch on Wednesday, and I guess we’ll evaluate then. I think the world of him. The baseball card looks great. But where we’re at, there’s got to be something for us to be able to hang our hat on. And he knows that. He knows that. He wants to pitch well. So for me, Wednesday, we’ll be watching closely.”
He also acknowledged that Diaz might not make the postseason roster.
“Yeah … we have to go with our best pitchers, as far as performance, talent, all that stuff. So my bet is that he will be (one of them). But again, there’s got to be some kind of evidence or something for us, again, to sort of bet on. My bet is yes, but we still have to see something.”
Fabian Ardaya of The Athletic has more on the terrible season overall that Diaz has had as a Dodger here.
The Dodgers are already down another reliever, at least for the rest of the regular season. Edgardo Henriquez went on the IL on Monday with lower back discomfort. Bobby Miller was recalled from Triple-A Oklahoma City. Right-hander Paul Gervase and left-hander Kris Bubic also joined the team in Cincinnati. Gervase was added to the active roster, and Bubic could be added in the coming days.
Roki Sasaki has been sidelines with a blister and is tentatively scheduled to pitch on Thursday in Cincinnati. However, the weather is supposed to be hot and humid, and the team is worried about how that will affect Sasaki’s blister.
“We just can’t put him in a position to go backward. And so obviously people can look at Thursday. But again, if he can’t do it without accomplishing it, finishing a start, and not regress, then it’s not worth it. So I think for us, we’re just keeping it open-ended right now.”

item.title: [MLB.com] Henriquez (back) hits IL, while Díaz's Triple-A struggles further complicate LA's bullpen woes
item.dc:creator: Sonja Chen
item.description: CINCINNATI -- At one point this season, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts proclaimed his "trust tree" of high-leverage bullpen arms to be as large as it had been in quite some time. But in the final two weeks before the postseason, his proverbial tree has grown far more bare. item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI -- At one point this season, Dodgers manager Dave Roberts proclaimed his "trust tree" of high-leverage bullpen arms to be as large as it had been in quite some time. But in the final two weeks before the postseason, his proverbial tree has grown far more bare.
The Dodgers lost hard-throwing right-hander Edgardo Henriquez, who had emerged as one of the team's most reliable relievers, to the 15-day injured list due to lower back discomfort before Monday's postseason-clinching 4-1 win over the Reds.
Henriquez is not eligible to return during the regular season, but the Dodgers are hopeful he could return for the playoffs. The team will know more after Henriquez undergoes imaging on his back and side.
The loss of Henriquez came after Roberts acknowledged that the rehabbing Edwin Díaz could be pitching himself out of a postseason bullpen role if he does not show improvement in what could be his final rehab outing with Triple-A Oklahoma City on Wednesday.
Right-handers Paul Gervase and Bobby Miller were recalled from Triple-A to shore up the bullpen on Monday.
As the most important games of the year draw near, the Dodgers' bullpen situation is starting to feel similar to last year, when they had more questions than answers for piecing together the late innings.
Henriquez posted a 2.85 ERA through 60 innings, striking out 71 against 25 walks. He hit 103 mph or higher 17 times, more than any Major League pitcher not named Jacob Misiorowski (140 pitches) or Mason Miller (33 pitches). But Henriquez became more than just a hard thrower this year, developing the command and the confidence to be a leverage weapon for the Dodgers.
With Díaz on the IL as he deals with inflammation on the right side of his neck, the Dodgers have not had a set closer, although Tanner Scott has gotten the bulk of save situations. Henriquez established himself as not only part of the bridge to the ninth inning, but also as a legitimate option to close out games.
"He’s got just really electric stuff, and in the ninth inning that stuff plays," Roberts said earlier this month. "In all honesty, there’s four or five guys that I feel can finish a game. But yeah, Edgardo is certainly high up the rungs."
The Dodgers have not seen enough from Díaz on his rehab assignment -- which was initially expected to span just a couple of outings -- to bring him back to the bullpen, further complicating the leverage picture.
Through four outings with Oklahoma City, Díaz has allowed six earned runs in 3 1/3 innings. He has struggled mightily with his command, issuing seven walks against four strikeouts. The hope was that he could use the stint in the Minors to work on his mechanical issues, but it is unclear whether he has made much progress.
Accordingly, it's questionable whether the Dodgers can afford to carry this version of Díaz on the postseason roster.
"We have to go with our best pitchers, as far as performance, talent, all that stuff," Roberts said. "My bet is that he will be [on the postseason roster]. But again, there's got to be some kind of evidence or something for us, again, to sort of bet on. So my bet is yes, but we still got to see something."
Díaz is on his second IL stint of the year after having surgery to remove loose bodies from his right elbow in April. In the first season of his three-year, $69 million contract with the Dodgers, Díaz has recorded an 11.85 ERA and blown four of his 11 save opportunities.
Roberts has already said that Díaz is set to pitch in lower leverage, rather than return to the closer role, when he's activated. If Díaz can earn back the ninth inning -- or any leverage opportunities -- it would partially solve the Dodgers' growing bullpen problem. But it comes down to whether he can perform when called on.
"He needs to pitch better. It hasn't been good," Roberts said. "He's going to pitch on Wednesday, and so I guess we'll evaluate then. I think the world of him. The baseball card looks great. But it's like, where we're at, there's got to be something for us to be able to hang our hat on. And he knows that. He wants to pitch well."

item.content:encoded:
By Field Level Media
Sep 15 (Field Level Media) – The Los Angeles Dodgers put relief pitcher Edgardo Henriquez on the 15-day injured list due to lower back discomfort on Monday, ending the right-hander’s regular season and causing more upheaval for the team’s bullpen.
Los Angeles has also been nursing Edwin Diaz back in a slow recovery from right elbow surgery with recent Triple-A outings that have not proven successful.
In his most recent appearance for Oklahoma City, Diaz struggled through two- thirds of an inning on Sunday, allowing five runs and three walks in a performance that Dodgers manager Dave Roberts admitted wasn’t going to be enough to merit a promotion.
The Dodgers have left open the possibility for Henriquez to return in the postseason.
Henriquez, 24, has appeared in 61 games (one start) this season, posting a 2.85 ERA with 71 strikeouts against 25 walks in 60 innings.
Diaz, a three-time All-Star, has struggled this season in limited action, logging seven saves in 11 opportunities and an 11.85 ERA in 16 appearances.
Los Angeles recalled right-handed pitchers Paul Gervase and Bobby Miller from Triple-A to help shore up their shaky bullpen. Emmet Sheehan was sent to Oklahoma City after throwing six shutout innings in a start against the Miami Marlins on Sunday.
Gervase, 26, has a 2.35 ERA over four major league appearances this season. He owns a lifetime 3.38 ERA with no decisions in 10 outings, all in relief, for the Tampa Bay Rays (2025) and Los Angeles (2025-26).
Miller, 27, has made one big-league appearance in 2026, earning a win over the Washington Nationals on Sept. 6 with three innings of one-run relief. He is 14-8 with a 5.40 ERA in 38 outings (36 starts) for the Dodgers over parts of four seasons.
Sheehan, 26, is 5-8 with a 4.79 ERA in 22 starts this year, 15-12 with a 4.23 ERA in 50 career appearances (45 starts), all with Los Angeles.
(–Field Level Media)

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Dodgers might be forced to leave Edwin Díaz off postseason roster
item.dc:creator: Maddie Lee

CINCINNATI — Even as the Dodgers clinched a postseason berth with their 4-1 win over the Reds on
item.content:encoded:
Dodgers might be forced to leave Edwin Díaz off postseason roster
- Click here to listen to this article
-
- Edwin Díaz struggled in his rehab start Sunday, and Dave Roberts is making it clear the Dodgers “got to see something” from the closer to put him on the playoff roster.
- The Dodgers placed reliever Edgardo Henriquez on the 15-day injured list and recalled Bobby Miller and Paul Gervase.
CINCINNATI — Even as the Dodgers clinched a postseason berth with their 4-1 win over the Reds on Monday, bullpen uncertainty loomed.
When they get to the playoffs, who’s going to take the ball in high-leverage situations?
Their options are dwindling. Edgardo Henriquez landed on the 15-day injured list Monday with low back discomfort, ruling him out for the rest of the regular season. Edwin Díaz was so shaky in his rehab assignment Sunday that a spot on the postseason roster isn’t guaranteed.
“We have to go with our best pitchers, as far as performance, talent, all that stuff,” manager Dave Roberts said before the Dodgers opened a four-game series against the Reds. “So my bet is that he will be [on the roster]. But there’s got to be some kind of evidence or something for us to sort of bet on. And so my bet is, yes, but we’ve still got to see something.”
The Dodgers clinch a playoff berth with their 4-1 victory over the Cincinnati Reds, reaching the postseason for a record-tying 14th consecutive year.
Díaz (neck) had the worst outing of his triple-A rehab assignment, surrendering five runs and issuing two walks in two-thirds of an inning. The dud put his return timeline in doubt. His next rehab appearance is scheduled for Wednesday.
“I think the world of him, the baseball card looks great,” Roberts said. “But where we’re at, there’s got to be something for us to be able to hang our hat on. And he knows that. He knows that. He wants to pitch well. So for me, Wednesday, we’ll be watching closely.”
So, who’s still in play?
Tanner Scott remains Roberts’ go-to in save situations. And Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips, Brock Stewart, Jack Dreyer and Blake Treinen all have experience in late innings.
On Monday, starter Tarik Skubal gave the group a much-needed break with seven shutout innings. He limited the Reds to three hits and a walk, cruising through their lineup almost three times in 90 pitches.
The Dodgers pulled ahead by four runs, on home runs from Kyle Tucker and Teoscar Hernández, who have both broken out of slumps, and an RBI single from Kiké Hernández.
With the game still relatively tight, Vesia entered in the bottom of the eighth to face the left-handed heavy bottom of the order. He retired the side.
Phillips and Treinen both were warming in the ninth when the Dodgers got a runner to second base with one out. When they failed to score him, Phillips jogged in to face the top of the order. He surrendered a high-flying solo homer to Elly De La Cruz on a fastball above the zone but avoided further damage.
Before the game, the Dodgers added two fresh arms to the bullpen. They recalled right-handers Bobby Miller and Paul Gervase, as they put Henriquez on the IL and optioned right-hander Emmet Sheehan.
Henriquez will undergo imaging on the area, which Roberts said stretched to his side near his oblique.
“The hope is we’ll get him back in the postseason,” Roberts said.
Roberts said he didn’t know what the move meant for Sheehan, who in his past two starts limited opponents to one run and recorded 15 strikeouts in a combined 11 ⅔ innings.
“Some of it’s probably contingent on Roki [Sasaki], and we’ve got another start coming up down the road here, as far as a bullpen kind of situation,” Roberts said. “So I don’t know, but Emmet’s done everything he can do in his power to force our hand, which I love. The last two have been really good.”
Sasaki (right middle finger blister) could start Thursday. His bullpen session Monday marked the first time he had tested covering the sensitive area on his finger with Dermabond, Roberts said.
“We just can’t put him in a position to go backward,” Roberts said.
The Dodgers also have more bullpen reinforcements coming.
Another bullpen addition is left-hander Kris Bubic, who met the team in Cincinnati and is in place to make his Dodgers debut later this week. Bubic made his last rehab appearance for triple-A Oklahoma City on Sunday, so Roberts said the Dodgers likely won’t activate him off the 60-day injured list until Wednesday at the earliest.
The Dodgers acquired Bubic from the Kansas City Royals at the trade deadline this year. He’d been on the IL since May, first with a low-grade flexor strain in his left forearm, and then a shoulder impingement setback.
In six triple-A rehab appearances over 5⅔ innings, Bubic didn’t yield a run and he limited opponents to two hits and two walks.
Roberts was noncommittal about Bubic being a high-leverage option.
“Seems like all of our games are leverage these days,” he said.
By not putting Shohei Ohtani on the injured list in July or in August, the Dodgers may have compromised the two-way star’s ability to be healthy for the playoffs.

item.content:encoded:
Claves: La rodilla de Freeman, el bate de Ohtani y el cálculo de octubre de Dodgers
CINCINNATI — Freddie Freeman no estuvo en la alineación de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles para el juego del lunes por la noche contra los Rojos de Cincinnati mientras lidia con molestias en la rodilla derecha.
Aunque el primera base no ha estado en la alineación en tres de los últimos cinco juegos, el mánager Dave Roberts manifestó que poner a Freeman en la lista de lesionados de 10 días para dejarlo listo para la postemporada —algo similar a lo que hicieron con Shohei Ohtani— no es una opción en este momento.
“No creo que (el descanso) tenga que ser de 10 días, pero ¿podría ser más de uno? Esa es una pregunta válida. Tengo que hablar un poco con el cuerpo de preparadores, con Freddie, y al final tomar esa decisión. Pero no creo que la lista de lesionados tenga sentido”, comentó Roberts.
Roberts señaló que no creía que Freeman fuera a tener problemas persistentes con la rodilla durante la postemporada si se puede manejar adecuadamente. Freeman batea para .293, pero está de 3 en sus últimos 30 turnos, con nueve ponches.
Los campeones defensores de la Serie Mundial por segundo año consecutivo llegaron al lunes por la noche con un número mágico de cuatro para asegurar su 13er título del Oeste de la Liga Nacional en 14 años. Su mayor preocupación es asegurarse de amarrar uno de los dos primeros puestos de preclasificación y un pase directo en la primera ronda.
Los Dodgers (90-59) llegaron al lunes con una ventaja de 2 1/2 juegos sobre Atlanta por el segundo puesto. Milwaukee (93-57) tiene la mejor marca de la Liga Nacional.
“Dado cómo están nuestros muchachos en cuanto a salud, conseguir esa semana sería enorme. Aun así, tenemos que jugar bien para cerrar la temporada y llegar a ese punto”, expresó Roberts.
Ohtani, quien ha estado en la lista de lesionados de 15 días desde el 8 de septiembre debido a una inflamación en el bíceps derecho, hará swings desde un tee en Los Ángeles el martes. Serán sus primeros swings desde que ingresó a la lista de lesionados. Roberts indicó que Ohtani ha estado levantando pesas, entrenando y recibiendo tratamiento en los últimos días.
Con Ohtani fuera del viaje de siete juegos, definitivamente ha habido un ambiente distinto en el clubhouse.
“Se siente diferente porque él tiene mucha presencia cuando está en el campo. La última serie no fue indicativa, pero creo que en general estamos jugando buen béisbol. Sabemos que somos mejores con Shohei. Probablemente los aficionados estén decepcionados, pero no creo que nosotros realmente lo hayamos sentido”, dijo Roberts.
La mayor preocupación podría estar con el relevista Edwin Díaz, quien ha permitido seis carreras limpias en 3 1/3 entradas en cuatro apariciones de rehabilitación con Triple-A Oklahoma City.
Díaz no solo está lidiando con una inflamación en el cuello, sino también con problemas de control. Díaz firmó un contrato de 59 millones de dólares por tres años durante la temporada baja y ha tenido dificultades en su primer año en Los Ángeles.
El derecho tendrá otra salida el miércoles, pero Roberts sí dejó abierta la posibilidad de que Díaz quede fuera de los rosters de postemporada.
“Necesita lanzar mejor. No ha sido bueno. La tarjeta de béisbol se ve genial. Pero, tal como estamos, tiene que haber algo a lo que podamos aferrarnos. Y él lo sabe. Quiere lanzar bien”, afirmó Roberts.
__

item.title: [The New York Times] Edwin Díaz continues to struggle, could be left off Dodgers’ postseason roster
item.dc:creator: Fabian Ardaya
item.description: CINCINNATI — The Los Angeles Dodgers set out this winter to address the closer position for good. Instead, they’re facing the possibility that a reliever they signed as a star free agent will be excluded from their postseason plans for a second consecutive season. Edwin Díaz continues to struggle, as Tanner Scott did a year ago, and his rehab assignment with Triple-A Oklahoma City has gone poorly enough that Dodgers manager Dave Roberts acknowledged Monday the club could leave the three-time All
item.content:encoded:
CINCINNATI — The Los Angeles Dodgers set out this winter to address the closer position for good. Instead, they’re facing the possibility that a reliever they signed as a star free agent will be excluded from their postseason plans for a second consecutive season.
Edwin Díaz continues to struggle, as Tanner Scott did a year ago, and his rehab assignment with Triple-A Oklahoma City has gone poorly enough that Dodgers manager Dave Roberts acknowledged Monday the club could leave the three-time All-Star closer off the postseason roster. Against minor-leaguers Sunday, Díaz surrendered five runs, walked three, hit a batter and recorded just two outs in his worst appearance yet.
Advertisement
“We have to go with our best pitchers, as far as performance, talent, all that stuff,” Roberts said. “So my bet is that he will be (on the roster). But again, there’s got to be some kind of evidence or something for us, again, to sort of bet on. And so my bet is yes, but we still got to see something.”
The Dodgers gave Díaz three years and $69 million to address a bullpen that floundered in 2025. They won their second consecutive World Series despite Scott — who signed a four-year, $72 million contract — not appearing in a single playoff game.
A second plunge into the deep end of the relief market brought even worse results than the 4.74 ERA and league-worst 10 blown saves Scott had in 2025. Díaz’s famous trumpets have sounded more like a sad trombone.
Díaz’s 16 appearances with the Dodgers yielded a disastrous 11.85 ERA. He missed three months due to arthroscopic surgery to remove loose bodies in his right elbow. Upon his return, he struggled enough that the Dodgers almost immediately put him back on the injured list for what they called a neck issue. They believed his struggles were mechanical, citing the lowest arm angle of his career (14.9 degrees) as a reason his stuff and command were nowhere near where they needed to be.
Attempts to correct the issue have not worked. What was supposed to be a pair of rehab outings has been extended. The organization thought Sunday’s outing could be the final step before activation, with Díaz joining the team in Cincinnati this week to try to re-earn his closer’s job.
But Díaz has allowed six runs and walked seven of the 21 batters he’s faced since starting his rehab. Even more concerning is how Díaz’s delivery seems even more out of whack than before. His fastball still lacks the north-south movement that it needs to succeed. On that pitch this season, he’s averaged 11.8 inches of induced vertical break, which measures how much “hop” or “ride” the pitch generates. The 15 fastballs he threw Sunday generated just 9.7 inches of IVB.
There’s plenty for Díaz to fix, and not a lot of time.
Advertisement
“He needs to pitch better,” Roberts said. “I think the world of him. The baseball card looks great. But it’s like, where we’re at, there’s got to be something for us to be able to hang our hat on. And he knows that. He knows that. He wants to pitch well.”
So the Dodgers summoned rehabbing reliever Kris Bubic to join the big club Monday instead. Bubic is expected to pitch as soon as Wednesday, Roberts said. Bubic, a former All-Star starting pitcher with the Kansas City Royals, was acquired at the trade deadline and has thrown 5 2/3 scoreless innings with nine strikeouts on his rehab assignment since the trade.
Díaz will stick with Oklahoma City for at least one more outing on Wednesday, and the organization will evaluate from there, Roberts said.
The Dodgers will spend the coming days trying to sort out how they will attack the ninth inning. One option went on the IL on Monday, when the Dodgers placed hard-throwing reliever Edgardo Henriquez on the shelf with a lower back issue; Henriquez has been the Dodgers’ most effective reliever recently, with a 1.69 ERA since Aug. 5. Now, his regular season is over.
Scott, who has bounced back this year with a 2.91 ERA, will be part of fixing the ninth-inning problem they thought they’d avoid entirely when they signed Díaz.
